title: docs: add an identity vetting predicate as a worked statement profile
body:
Builds on #47. A worked example of a community-defined predicate, added after **Community-Defined Predicates**.

**Why this replaces #49.** #49 profiled the VEC for identity vetting, with the reasoning "why a VEC and not a new credential type". That was wrong, and the objection is the obvious one: a *Verifiable Endorsement Credential* is for endorsing. A vetting statement is a record of a procedure — a named member checked an applicant's claimed identity, by a stated method, against stated classes of document, on a stated date. Pressing the endorsement envelope into that service is renaming, not modelling. #47 is exactly the mechanism that makes it unnecessary, so vetting becomes its own predicate instead. I'll close #49 in favour of this.

**What it adds.** One informative subsection. The payload #49 carried in the `endorsement` body moves unchanged into the statement's `object.value`: `community`, `method`, `documentClasses`, `claimsVerified`, `livenessConfirmed`, `identityCommitment`, `cardDigestMultibase`, `declaredRelationship`, `attestationTextDigest`. It states all nine items [Predicate Profiles](#predicate-profiles) requires, including what a pass does and does not establish — notably that it establishes nothing about whether the claimed identity is *true*, whether the vetter was eligible, or whether anyone has been admitted.

**A difficulty that dissolves.** #49 needed an editor's note asking whether a vetting exchange satisfies the VEC's "one party to a DTG edge" language, since vetter and applicant often share no edge and the applicant is not yet a member. A statement annotates a node, so the question no longer arises and the note is gone.

**Namespace.** The predicate sits in a community namespace (`https://vtc.example/vocab/vetting/v1#vetted`), matching the existing community-predicate example and the editor's note that this specification defines mechanisms rather than naming predicates. If more than one community adopts it, it is a candidate for promotion into the planned vocabulary — the path your note already describes.

**Validation.** `npm run render` completes cleanly and writes `docs/index.html`. The five dangling definitions it reports (CTA, PNV, personal trust network, relationship invitation, VTC trust anchor) are unreferenced on the base branch too, so they are not from this change. One term reference is used, `[[ref: VMC]]`.

**One observation, not addressed here.** Section links of the form `](#vsc-verifiable-statement-credential)` do not resolve: the renderer emits ids with the parentheses, `id="vsc-(verifiable-statement-credential)"`. Six such links already exist on the base branch, so my new link follows the same house form rather than diverging in one place. Worth a separate fix across the document if you agree.

Based on `feat/verifiable-statement-credential`, so it should merge after #47. Happy to rebase onto `main` instead if that lands differently.

title: Record tasks that require a proof and are served on a bearer token
body:
Adds three *observed* entries to F.2. Each one covers a single kind of behaviour, so there is no row per task.

## Tasks that require a proof, served only on a bearer token

**VTI-OPS-020, VTI-OPS-021, VTI-OPS-024, VTI-OPS-093.** One community node serves 47 tasks whose own definitions declare `proofRequirement: REQUIRED` over an HTTP binding that carries **no operation document**:

- the body is the bare payload;
- the task is named in a header and checked against the route;
- a bearer session token authenticates the caller.

So no proof is verified, and no time of issue is checked. For all but six of these tasks the definition also declares `issuedAtRequirement: REQUIRED`. No document identifier reaches the replay record either.

The set, taken from the node's route table and the definitions' front matter:

- **30 community tasks.** 18 are administrative, for example `vtc/members/{credentials, update, admin-remove, purge}`, `vtc/join-requests/decide` and `vtc/backup/{export, import}`. 12 are taken under a member's session, for example `vtc/members/{renew, rotate, personhood/assert}`, `vtc/endorsements/issue` and `vtc/invitations/issue`.
- **17 canonical tasks shared with other node types:** `acl/*`, `config/*`, `policy/*`, `audit/list`, and `auth/*` including the passkey management tasks.
- **`vtc/auth/admin-session`**, which takes an access token in the body.

The full list is in the entry.

The intended resolution is to bind each of these tasks in the document dispatcher, with the proof verified and the time of issue checked. The bearer route stays only as a documented transitional path with a stated removal point. The rationale comes from the HTTPS binding's own §5 (transport security profile) and SPEC §9.1.1: a bearer token authenticates whoever presents it, not the party who composed the request.

## The dispatcher does not enforce the requirement either

**VTI-OPS-021, VTI-OPS-024.** The same node's document dispatcher verifies a proof whenever one is present. When the proof is absent, it takes attribution from the transport, including for tasks that declare the proof REQUIRED (joining, self-removal, `members/vmc`, vetting grant and statement revocation, and personhood assertion). It applies no acceptance window to `issuedAt`.

This is an observed instance of the existing *reported* VTI-OPS-021 row. It is recorded next to the first entry because that entry's resolution, moving tasks into the dispatcher, closes nothing until this one is resolved.

## Admin promotion through a task that refuses it

**VTI-OPS-110, VTI-OPS-051.** The definition of `vtc/members/update` refuses `role: admin` with `adminRoleForbidden` and leaves promotion to a separate, gated operation. The same node promotes through that task instead. A passkey step-up checked in the handler gates it, and the node's administration console depends on that path. So the declared code is never emitted.

The node also serves `acl/change-role`, the operation defined for role transitions, and `acl/grant`. Both assign the administrative role with no step-up, so the handler's gate does not bound promotion.

The intended resolution is to move promotion to `acl/change-role`, with the step-up enforced by the policy gate, point the console there, and then refuse `role: admin` on `members/update`. The step-up has to land on the role-change operation before the console moves. Tracked in OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1645.

## What this is not

It is not a change proposal. No entry qualifies the requirement it is listed against (VTI-CNF-014).

## Build

`npm run render` completes, and all three rows render as table rows.

title: Bind taskContext to the published Trust Tasks mechanisms, and secure credentials with Data Integrity
body:
The credential-side half of splitting #18 across the three specifications, as planned on #18 once the VTI repository existed. **#18 stays open until these three merge**, then closes pointing at them.

| Part | PR |
|---|---|
| Credentials (this PR) | this one |
| Trust Tasks | trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-spec#15 |
| VTI | trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#33 |
| Executable evidence | [Keyring `ref-07g-outcome-evidence-pairing`](https://github.com/berkmancenter/keyring-wallet/tree/c3a7f1d2a547d7a602cf93b87f5672d7a158d4c1/tsp-reference/ref-07g-outcome-evidence-pairing) |

**Merge order.** trust-tasks-spec#15, which this PR links to, is merged and its review continues in trust-tasks-spec#17; this PR waits on that review. It and the VTI PR can merge in either order after it.

@talltree @sankarshanmukhopadhyay — tagging you as the authors of the #39 scope guidance this split implements, and @talltree for the review on #18 that asked for it. @stormer78 — the Trust Tasks PR carries your trust-tasks-tf#173 follow-ups.

## How the split was decided

Two rules already on the record, applied as written:

- **Scope guidance** from [dtgwg-cred-tf discussion #39](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-tf/discussions/39) (Drummond, agreed by Sankarshan): credentials define types, properties and high-level requirements and *reference* the other specifications; Trust Tasks defines processing, ceremony and evidence requirements. VTI, created afterwards, owns what holds only across a composition.
- **The review on #18**: Trust Task Context Binding detail belongs in the Trust Tasks specification; ZK proof types do not belong in the credential specification.

And one rule for this split: everything in #18 is carried unless other work has already superseded it.

## Where each part of #18 went

| #18 content | Now |
|---|---|
| `digestMultibase` for the VWC | **Already on main** (#19) |
| `z`/`u` multibase headers | **Superseded** — main requires base58btc `z` only |
| Framework 0.4 permalinks; the "Trust Tasks core specification" term | **Dropped** — the framework is published; cited directly |
| "id locates, digest binds"; `proofValue` rejected as binder | **Already in Trust Tasks 0.5.0** (via trust-tasks-tf#173) — cited |
| `taskContext` = innermost exchange's initiating `id` | **This PR** — property definition, citing Trust Tasks |
| `taskDigestMultibase` | **This PR** — Base Structure, `dtg:witnessed` profile, profile item 6 |
| `DataIntegrityProof` + `eddsa-jcs-2022` RECOMMENDED | **This PR** — `proof` property and examples |
| `bbs-2023`, proof sets, selective-disclosure trade-off | **Not carried** — outside the credential spec per the #18 review; this PR only states that a selective-disclosure mechanism is carried in addition to the proof |
| Qualifying Trust Task specification profile | **Trust Tasks** — Specification Requirements item 20, updated with the three changes from trust-tasks-tf#173 |
| Pairing checklist; errors as failure evidence | **Trust Tasks** — *Evidence That a Cited Exchange Completed* |
| Holder ships outcome evidence | **This PR** (holder MUST), **Trust Tasks** (SHOULD carry), **VTI** (VTI-CMP-023) |
| Verifier MUST NOT infer completion | **This PR** keeps it, pointing at Trust Tasks and VTI |
| Related Specifications; #11 | **This PR** and **VTI** (citations fixed both ways) |

## What changed here

- **`taskContext`** is the initiating document's `id` of the innermost attesting exchange. Base Structure said `threadId`, which contradicts the published Trust Tasks rule.
- **`taskDigestMultibase`** is defined. `witness/session/submit/0.1` and `vetting/session/0.1` already require it and say its schema *"belongs to DTG Core Credentials"*.
- **Outcome Interpretability** keeps its MUST NOT and points at the Trust Tasks checks and VTI; the holder conformance item follows.
- **Related Specifications** lists Trust Tasks and VTI as published; DTG Core Trust Task Protocols stays planned for DTG-specific task specifications. The two remaining "planned Protocols" mentions (VMC lifecycle, VDC invocation) are untouched — their referents still don't exist. Resolves #11.
- **`proof`** is `DataIntegrityProof` with `eddsa-jcs-2022` RECOMMENDED; all examples updated (#17 item 3).
- **Minimum compatible version** keeps `0.4.0` for naming and binding, with the outcome-evidence minimum recorded as pending until trust-tasks-spec#15 is released under a Document Status.

## Behaviour change for verifiers

**Outcome evidence now travels with the presentation.** The previous Outcome Interpretability text let a verifier locate outcome evidence through `taskContext` (*"or the `taskContext` value enables the verifier to locate it"*). That path is gone: a holder presenting the credential as evidence of completion MUST include the outcome evidence, and a verifier that does not receive it MUST treat the credential as not evidencing completion. This follows the Trust Tasks specification, which puts discovering and retrieving outcome evidence out of scope, but it changes what a verifier that relied on looking the evidence up can conclude.

## Found while splitting — recorded, not addressed here

1. **#18's own text rejects the real witness ceremony.** "The originating request's Type URI with `#response`" can't match `witness/session` → `witness/session/submit#response`. The Trust Tasks PR replaces it with a declared outcome-evidence type ([rung](https://github.com/berkmancenter/keyring-wallet/tree/c3a7f1d2a547d7a602cf93b87f5672d7a158d4c1/tsp-reference/ref-07g-outcome-evidence-pairing), Act 4).
2. **Keyring's verifier accepts a cancelled session's control `#response` and a holder-signed `#response` as completion** ([rung](https://github.com/berkmancenter/keyring-wallet/tree/c3a7f1d2a547d7a602cf93b87f5672d7a158d4c1/tsp-reference/ref-07g-outcome-evidence-pairing), Act 3). A Keyring fix, not a spec one.
3. **The witness spec's "evidence issuer is the credential issuer" does not generalize** — vetting's response is signed by the applicant, not the vetter who issues the statement. The Trust Tasks rule uses the initiating document's `recipient`.
4. **VTI uses "witness" only for a DID-log host service**, while a VWC witness issues credentials. Worth a terminology pass at some point; nothing here depends on it.
5. **The minimum-version values stay pending** until the Trust Tasks definition is released under a Document Status.

## For review

- Reviewed internally on our fork before proposing here; @bmiller59 is credited as co-author for the #15 material redistributed into this PR.
- Rendered with `npm run render` — no errors, every new anchor resolves.
- Open PRs #55 and #50 touch `spec/body.md` as well; I checked this branch merges cleanly with both, and the anchors this PR references survive #55's restructuring.

title: Bind taskContext to the published Trust Tasks mechanisms, and secure credentials with Data Integrity (#56)
body:
Bind taskContext to the published Trust Tasks mechanisms, and secure credentials with Data Integrity (#56)

* Bind taskContext to the published Trust Tasks mechanisms, and secure credentials with Data Integrity

The credential-side half of the #18 split. Following the working group's
scope guidance — a credential specification defines its types, properties
and high-level requirements, and references the Trust Tasks and VTI
specifications for exchange processing and composition — this keeps the
properties here and points at the specifications that now define the rest.

Trust Task Context Binding
- taskContext is the id of the innermost attesting exchange's initiating
  document, per the Trust Tasks specification's "Naming an Exchange from
  Outside the Framework". Base Structure previously said threadId, which
  contradicts that published rule.
- New taskDigestMultibase property: the task digest of that document, per
  "Binding a Citation to the Document It Names". The witness/session/submit
  and vetting/session registry specifications already require it on the
  credential and state that its schema belongs to this specification.
- Outcome Interpretability keeps its MUST NOT, and now points at the Trust
  Tasks specification's outcome-evidence checks (proposed alongside this
  change) and at VTI for what a relying party may conclude across a
  composition. Holders presenting a credential as evidence of completion
  include the outcome evidence; the conformance holder item follows.
- The dtg:witnessed profile requires both properties, and its example uses an
  id-shaped taskContext rather than a thread label. Profile item 6 names both.
- The minimum-compatible-version note keeps 0.4.0 for naming and binding and
  records the outcome-evidence minimum as pending.

Related specifications (resolves #11)
- Trust Tasks and VTI are listed as published companions; DTG Core Trust
  Task Protocols remains planned for DTG-specific task specifications, but
  is no longer where outcome evidence is defined. The nesting rule and the
  credential/artifact boundary cite the Trust Tasks specification.

Proofs (#17 item 3)
- proof is a DataIntegrityProof with the suite in proof.cryptosuite;
  eddsa-jcs-2022 is RECOMMENDED because it needs no @context resolution at

title: Keep credential validity and exchange completion apart (#33)
body:
Keep credential validity and exchange completion apart (#33)

* Keep credential validity and exchange completion apart across the composition

The VTI half of the cred-spec #18 split. A DTG credential can cite the Trust
Task exchange that attests it (taskContext), and whether that exchange
completed is decided over documents the credential does not contain. The
credential specification owns validity and the Trust Tasks specification owns
the outcome-evidence checks; that a relying party does not read the first as
the second holds only across their composition, which this specification
owns.

- VTI-CMP-022: a credential citing an exchange is not evidence the exchange
  completed without outcome evidence satisfying the Trust Tasks checks.
- VTI-CMP-023: where a decision depends on completion, the outcome evidence
  travels with the presentation; without it, the credential is not reported
  as evidencing completion.
- VTI-CMP-064: outcome evidence counts among the durable correlators under
  VTI-CMP-062 — whole Trust Task documents disclose the exchange's and both
  parties' identifiers regardless of the credential's own proof mechanism.
- VTI-CRD-032: successful credential verification does not establish
  completion; pointer to VTI-CMP-022.
- References: the [DTG-CRED] and [TRUST-TASKS] citations are fixed, and the
  intro's cross-specification note records the minimum Document Status of
  each as pending the release of the definitions this depends on.
- Appendix E, Family 2, as VTI-CMP-120 requires for new composition
  requirements: propositions, counter-cases, JOINTLY-OWNED, with an
  executable pressure test in Keyring's tsp-reference for the second.

Requirement identifiers follow the section blocks already in use and may be
renumbered by the editor.

Refs trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec#18, trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec#11.

Appendix E's Family 2 entry carries an inline note that issue #32 questions
whether that appendix should be reclassified or restructured; the entry moves
with it if so, rather than holding this change on it.

title: Keep credential validity and exchange completion apart
body:
The VTI half of splitting [trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec#18](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec/pull/18) across the three specifications, following the scope guidance in [dtgwg-cred-tf#39](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-tf/discussions/39). The full redistribution map is in the credentials PR.

| Part | PR |
|---|---|
| VTI (this PR) | this one |
| Trust Tasks | trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-spec#15 |
| Credentials | trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec#56 |

**Merge order: trust-tasks-spec#15 first.** This PR cites the *Evidence That a Cited Exchange Completed* section that PR adds, through `[TRUST-TASKS]`. This PR and the credentials one can merge in either order once it is in.

@talltree @sankarshanmukhopadhyay — tagging you as the authors of the #39 scope guidance this split implements. @stormer78 — the Trust Tasks PR carries your trust-tasks-tf#173 follow-ups.

## Why here

Credential validity is decided under the credential specification; whether the exchange a credential cites completed is decided under Trust Tasks, over documents the credential does not contain. Keeping a relying party from reading the first as the second is a property of the composition — the kind VTI-CMP-001 says this specification owns.

## What this adds

- **VTI-CMP-022 / 023** (Semantic completion) — a credential citing an exchange is not completion evidence without outcome evidence satisfying the Trust Tasks checks; where a decision depends on completion, the evidence travels with the presentation.
- **VTI-CMP-064** (Privacy across composition) — outcome evidence counts among the durable correlators of VTI-CMP-062: whole Trust Task documents disclose the exchange's and both parties' identifiers regardless of the credential's own proof mechanism.
- **VTI-CRD-032** — successful credential verification does not establish completion; pointer to VTI-CMP-022.
- **References** — the `[DTG-CRED]` and `[TRUST-TASKS]` citations are fixed; the intro's cross-specification note records the minimum Document Status of each as pending the release of the definitions this depends on.
- **Appendix E, Family 2** — required by VTI-CMP-120 for new composition requirements: propositions, counter-cases, `JOINTLY-OWNED`, and [Keyring `ref-07g`](https://github.com/berkmancenter/keyring-wallet/tree/c3a7f1d2a547d7a602cf93b87f5672d7a158d4c1/tsp-reference/ref-07g-outcome-evidence-pairing) as the pressure test for the second proposition.

## Notes for review

- **Requirement identifiers** follow the numbering blocks already in use in each section; the editor may renumber.
- **Appendix E and #32.** Family 2 is recorded here as VTI-CMP-120 currently requires, with Appendix E in its present (informative) form. #32 questions whether that appendix should be reclassified or restructured; if it is, this entry moves with it. The entry carries that note inline.
- **Terminology, not addressed here:** this specification uses "witness" for a DID-log host service, while a witnessed credential's witness issues credentials. Worth a pass at some point; nothing in this PR depends on it.
- Rendered with `npm run render` — no errors, no duplicate identifiers.
- Reviewed internally on our fork before proposing here; @bmiller59 is credited as co-author, and the Appendix E note is his.

title: fix(vtc): emit the error codes the admin, backup, directory, endorsement and install tasks declare (#1600, part 2)
body:
Refs #1600

This follows #1644 and covers the families it did not reach: admin/bootstrap, admin/invites, backup, community profile, config import, directory, endorsement-types, endorsements and install. Each handler now emits the code its specification declares. Each code has a witness test and is removed from the census baseline.

**Baseline: 39 → 12.** (88 declared in scope. 76 are now witnessed, up from 49.)

## How

This uses #1644's mechanism with no changes. The handler returns `crate::error::TaskError`, and `TaskError::declared(<generated …::error_codes::X.code>, <the AppError it already had>)` attaches the code. Every route in this PR is REST-only, so each response keeps the inner error's status and `error` member and gains a `code` member. Every constant comes from `trust_tasks_rs::specs::vtc::…::error_codes::X.code`, both in the handlers and in the tests. None is written as a string literal.

To let the census name the handler constants, `routes::{admin, community, directory, endorsement_types}` are now `pub(crate)`.

## Codes emitted (all needed a handler change)

| Task | Codes | Situation |
|---|---|---|
| admin/bootstrap | invalidToken, alreadyBootstrapped | setup-session token fails to decode (bad signature, wrong audience, expired) / an Admin ACL row already exists |
| admin/invites/create | ttlTooLong | `ttlSeconds` > 24 h. A zero TTL is the same 400 with no code, because only the upper bound is declared. |
| admin/invites/revoke | notFound | unknown `jti`, including the race where the row disappears between the check and the delete |
| backup/export | passwordTooShort | password below `MIN_BACKUP_PASSWORD_LEN` |
| backup/import | decryptionFailed | AES-GCM tag failure: wrong password or altered ciphertext. Envelope shape errors stay 400 with no code. |
| community/profile/update | validationFailed | any `Validation` refusal from `CommunityProfileUpdate::apply` |
| config/import | unsupportedSchemaVersion, communityDidMismatch | the two existing refusals |
| directory/query | notFound | see behaviour changes |
| endorsement-types/register | invalidUri, reserved, exists | empty or blank URI, or over 512 bytes / `CommunityRole` / already registered |
| endorsement-types/delete | notFound, inUse | the two existing refusals |
| endorsements/issue | typeNotRegistered, claimTooLarge, claimSchemaViolation, statusListExhausted | see behaviour changes for claimSchemaViolation |
| endorsements/list | invalidCursor | cursor fails to decode or verify |
| endorsements/show | notFound | unknown id |
| endorsements/revoke | notFound, alreadyRevoked | see behaviour changes |
| install/claim/start | invalidToken | token parse failure, and the install state machine's `Unauthorized` refusals (not found / consumed / expired) |
| install/claim/finish | invalidToken, registrationMismatch, bindingInvalid | token as for start, plus consumed with no admin persisted / `registrationId` that is not a UUID, names another enrolment, or has no open enrolment / `finish_passkey_registration` fails |

Refusals that are not token faults stay undeclared: the claim-secret 401s (`claim_secret_required` / `claim_secret_invalid`, which the install page reads from `error`) and the concurrent-ceremony 409.

## Behaviour changes worth reviewing

**No REST status changed except the two the specifications require (directory and endorsements/revoke, below).** Every other status in the table is the one the route returned before.

- **endorsements/revoke: re-revoking now answers 409 `alreadyRevoked`. It used to answer 200 with the first receipt.** revoke/0.1 Conformance 3 requires this: the spec says "implementations MUST adopt the error" and names the silent 200 as the pre-migration divergence. The status-list bit is not re-flipped and no audit envelope is written. Callers checked: the admin UI (`revokeGrant`, `revokeVetterRole`) and `vtc-client::revoke_endorsement` / `cnm vetting vetters revoke` only revoke live grants. A double-click now shows an error toast instead of a second success. `revoke_idempotent_on_already_revoked` is replaced by `re_revoking_is_the_declared_already_revoked`, which also checks that no audit row is added.
- **endorsements/issue now enforces the endorsement type's `claimSchema`** (`claimSchemaViolation`, 400). Registration has always stored `claimSchema`, but nothing read it back, so any claim was accepted. Issue/0.1 Conformance 3 requires the validation. A type whose stored schema is not itself valid JSON Schema now fails issuance with 500. That is the registration's fault, not the claim's. Registration does not validate the schema yet.
- **directory/query: three outcomes now give one answer, 404 `notFound` with one message.** Those outcomes are a subject who is not a member, a policy deny, and an allow whose projection is empty. Before, a non-member subject answered 200 with only `{did}`, and a deny answered 403 with the policy's deny code in the message. The spec's Conformance section requires "notFound rather than an empty projection", and its Security section calls a distinguishable "exists but you may see nothing" a membership oracle. The deny code is now logged at debug level and no longer sent to the caller. Nothing in `admin-ui/src` or `vtc-client` calls this route, apart from the generated `wire.ts` type. `non_member_subject_projects_did_only`, which pinned the old 200, is replaced.
- **install/claim/finish: the message for a `registrationId` that is not a UUID changed** from "invalid install token (malformed jti)" to "registration_id does not match install token". The status is still 401. The admin UI does not match on either string.
- `admin-ui/openapi.json` and `wire.ts` are regenerated. They show directory 403 → 404 and the new revoke 409. There are no type changes, and `npm run lint` and vitest pass.

## Security-relevant fixes

- **endorsements/revoke checks the caller's capability before looking up the id.** Before, the 404 for an unknown id came before the Admin/Issuer check. Any authenticated caller, even one with no ACL row, could tell which endorsement ids exist from 404 versus 403. The order now follows Conformance 1 before 2, and a member gets 403 whether the id exists or not. `an_unknown_endorsement_is_the_declared_not_found` asserts this.
- **directory/query is no longer a membership oracle** (described above). A deny for an existing subject and a missing subject now return the same status, code and body. `nothing_visible_is_indistinguishable_from_no_such_member` compares the two bodies byte for byte.
- **endorsements/issue now enforces `claimSchema`** (described above). An Issuer could previously sign a claim that broke the type's declared shape, under the community's key.

## Left baselined (12)

**In these families: needs a design decision**
- `admin/invites/revoke:alreadyConsumed`. revoke/0.1 says a consumed invite MUST be refused because it is immutable audit history. This service deletes consumed rows on purpose: the handler comment says the audit trail is the `CommunityInstalled` envelope, not the install-store row. The admin UI's **Remove** action on consumed and expired rows depends on that. Emitting the code means removing that UI action and deciding where consumed rows are pruned, so it belongs in the divergence register. The handler comment now names the divergence.

**Spec vs implementation, recorded but not changed**
- `backup/export:passwordTooShort`: the spec names a 12-character minimum. This service uses the workspace's `MIN_BACKUP_PASSWORD_LEN` (15). The code is emitted below 15. A stricter floor is not lowered to match the spec, so the spec's figure should be corrected.
- `endorsement-types/delete:inUse` declares a `detailsSchema` (`liveEndorsements`, `criteria`). The REST error body has no `details` slot in #1644's mechanism, so the message names both instead, as it already did. The route is REST-only, so no Trust Task `details` is lost.
- `endorsements/issue:statusListExhausted` is `retryable: true` but still answers the 500 it always did. The status was kept unchanged.

**Out of scope for this PR (not attempted)**
- `vtc/invitations/*` (2) is owned by another session.
- `vtc/auth/*` (5) was left alone because auth is being changed elsewhere (#1646 landed during this work).
- `join-requests/submit:policyUnsatisfied`, `members/update:adminRoleForbidden`, `vetting/revoke-statement:issuerMismatch` / `:digestMismatch` are still waiting for the design decisions described in #1644.

## Tests

Run after rebasing onto `1f6025ea` (#1646):

- `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --no-fail-fast`, with the admin-UI build on (`VTC_SKIP_ADMIN_UI_BUILD` unset): pass. 1825 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored, across 67 test binaries.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: pass
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: pass
- `admin-ui`: `npm run lint` (wire:check + tsc) pass; `npm test` (vitest) 168/168 pass

Only vtc-service changed (source, tests, `admin-ui/openapi.json`, `admin-ui/src/lib/wire.ts`). There are no vta-sdk, vti-common or vtc-client edits, so the workspace job was not run.

title: feat(persona): wear a face without naming a persona DID
body:
Design note (VTI docs/05-design-notes/persona-context-first.md) §9.7: a
holder should say "wear this face here", not bring a DID.

binding/set: `personaDid` becomes optional. Omitted, the maintainer uses
the persona the holder already uses in the context — the one DID with a
binding there, current or cleared — and names it in the response. None
is refused (`noPersonaHere`); several are refused (`personaAmbiguous`,
naming them), since choosing one would decide which of the holder's
identities a context sees.

profile/compose: `wear: true` wears the new face the same way;
`wearAndPersona` refuses it alongside `personaDid`. `label` and `until`
now need the face worn by either route.

Neither task mints a persona. A DID has a lifecycle of its own — keys,
hosting, services — and a write that could half-create one would leave a
published identity nobody holds; personas are minted first, through the
DID-template path.

title: feat(vtc): deliver an invitation to the DID it admits — pushed as an offer, or as a QR
body:
Keyring VTI-21 and VTI-32, implementing `vtc/invitations/deliver/0.1` (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#581, released in trust-tasks-rs 0.21.15).

`vtc/invitations/issue` returned the signed invitation to the inviter **once**, and nothing carried it further. The admin console tried to show it as a QR code, and it was too large to fit.

## Delivery

`POST /v1/invitations/deliver` (inviter roles: Admin, Moderator or Issuer) records a **single-use OID4VCI offer** for the invitation. The offer is bound to the invited DID, and delivering again withdraws the previous one. Then, depending on the channel:

- **`message`:** the offer is sent to the invited DID as a `credential-exchange/offer` over DIDComm, through the community's mediator, the same path members already get credentials on. `noRoute` (422) means the DID doesn't resolve to a key-agreement key to encrypt to. An advertised service isn't required: a `did:peer:2` holding only keys is reachable. If the send fails, the offer is withdrawn.
- **`offer`:** the offer is returned to the inviter. It *names* the credential rather than containing it, so it fits in a QR code as an `openid-credential-offer://` link.

## Redemption: the invited DID's key, and nothing else

The invitation is released only through `credential-exchange/request`, with a key-binding proof made by **the invited DID's key**. A photographed QR code or a misdirected message admits no one else. Two changes were needed to make that hold:

- **Any DID method.** Key-binding proofs used to accept only `did:key` holders ("a follow-up slice"), so a `did:webvh` persona could receive an offer and never redeem it. The `kid` now resolves through the community's DID resolver (`DidVmResolver`), and `redeem` / `issue_on_request` take the resolver.
- **HTTPS redemption.** `POST /v1/credential-exchange/request` is for an invitee with no messaging service. It's unauthenticated, because the proof is the authority, and it sits on the rate-limited, body-capped chain (classified in `GOVERNED_UNAUTH`). It answers with the `credential-exchange/issue` payload that a messaging binding would send on-thread.

## Also

- **Stored invitations:** the signed invitation is now kept on its registry row so it can be delivered later. The list never shows it, because it builds each row field by field. Invitations issued before this change can't be delivered, and the route says to reissue them.
- **Declared error codes:** `notFound`, `revoked` and `noRoute` come from the generated `error_codes` and are emitted as `{"error","code"}`, witnessed for the #1600 census. There's also a conformance entry.
- **Why the URI is a literal:** `deliver` is bound in `routes/mod.rs` with a literal URI, as its siblings are. The census, the conformance sweep and the admin-UI manifest test all find bound tasks by scanning for literals, so a `TYPE_URI` binding would have been invisible to all three.
- **Admin console:** each live invitation gets **Send** and **QR offer** buttons, and the "too large for a QR code" message points to the offer.
- **Audit:** a new `AuditEvent::InvitationDelivered` (the enum is `#[non_exhaustive]`).
- **Dependencies:** the workspace requires trust-tasks-rs 0.21.15.

## Known divergence

`vtc/invitations/deliver/0.1` declares `proof: REQUIRED`. This route, like its siblings `vtc/invitations/{issue,revoke}`, is served as bearer-JWT REST, with no document proof, no `issuedAt` window and no replay record. That puts it in class 1 of the Appendix F.2 divergence recorded in trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#35 and tracked in #1641. A fix for that class across the VTC's REST tasks would cover this route too; this PR doesn't make it worse.

## Tests

- `tests/invitations.rs`:
  - an offered invitation is redeemed over HTTPS by the invitee's key, **once**;
  - another DID's proof is refused (403), and the offer still redeems for the invitee;
  - a new delivery withdraws the last code;
  - `noRoute`, `notFound` and `revoked` are asserted on the declared codes, and a non-inviter is refused.
- `tests/join_didcomm.rs` (didcomm-harness): the `message` channel's offer reaches the invited DID over the mediator.
- `credentials::exchange`: a `did:web` holder redeems through the resolver, the `did:key`-only verifier still refuses it, and the same proof can't redeem a credential bound to another DID.
- Admin console: `offerDeepLink` round-trips and fits a QR code. All 170 console tests, lint and `wire:check` pass.
- Full run before the last rebase: workspace 4756 / 0, vtc-service + vtc-client 1787 / 0, harness 4 / 0. After rebasing onto #1642, #1644 and #1646, I re-ran clippy `-D warnings` plus the census, conformance, unauth classification, exchange, invitation, manifest, OpenAPI snapshot and harness tests, and all pass.

title: feat(persona): make a face for a community, retire and reinstate faces, and read where a face has been
body:
The TUI side of verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1623, #1628 and #1635 (design note `persona-context-first.md` §5.3, §9.4, §9.6), on vta-sdk 0.48.

**Faces tab**
- `x` retires the selected face after a prompt that says how many communities it comes off and that it is kept with its history. `z` shows the retired faces; `x` there reinstates one — no question, since reinstating binds and removes nothing.
- An opened face says where it may be worn (its reach) and, from `profile/get` `disclosedTo`, how far it has spoken. `h` shows where it is worn now (with any end) and its timeline — made, worn, taken off, told whom which types, values changed, retired — types and parties only.
- The delete prompt carries "It has disclosed to N parties across M communities — deleting it does not un-tell them", read from the open face or asked for when it is armed, and points at `x` to retire instead when a persona wears the face.

**Communities tab**
- `c` makes a face for the selected community and wears it there as the persona that community sees. Local by default: ⇥ moves between fields, ↓ on the last adds a value, Ctrl-T marks a value "used in my other faces too". Half rows, malformed claim types and an empty face are refused on the form. The outcome says whether the face lives in that community alone, and when a shared value was already kept.

**Core** — `openvtc-core` `persona::lifecycle`: `compose`, `retire`, `reinstate`, `list_retired`, `history` (the timeline read to the end), `untell_words`. `ProfileSummary` gains `retired` and `reach_only`; `ProfileDetail` gains `disclosed_to`. The pane's read loads the retired faces with their own result, so a failure there shows in that view and does not blank the faces the holder wears.

Promote ("make a value reusable") stays in the console (vta-browser-plugin#268): the TUI does not list the context-local faces it acts on.

Verified locally with the CI set: fmt, both clippy runs, docs, `cargo test --workspace -- --include-ignored` (1499), `--no-default-features` (1480), `-p openvtc --features dev-overrides` (671), bench build.

title: fix(proof): verify the document as received, and only keys the DID authorises for signing
body:
Two defects in `trust-tasks-proof`'s `affinidi` verifier, found while building the Affinidi messaging mediator's Trust Task acceptance checks. The mediator currently works around both in its own code; this PR fixes them at the source so every consumer gets them. ## 1. `verify` checked a re-serialised document, not the one received `ProofVerifier::verify(&TrustTask

)` rebuilt the JSON from the parsed, typed document before checking the signature. The proof covers the JCS canonicalisation of the document **as the signer serialised it**, so any member whose serde round-trip isn't byte-exact breaks a genuine proof. Examples: an `issuedAt` written `+00:00` re-renders as `Z`; a number re-renders differently; a member unknown to `P` is dropped. - **New:** `Verifier::verify_raw(&serde_json::Value)` verifies over the document exactly as received. A receiver holding the raw JSON should call it. - **Changed:** `verify` now serialises the typed document and delegates to `verify_raw`, so its behaviour is unchanged. - **Same checks either way:** a proof is present and well-formed; issuer binding (SPEC §4.8, exact string equality); then the signature. ## 2. The resolver accepted any key in the document, and only Multikey keys `CachedDidResolver` took any `verificationMethod` whose id matched, including a key listed only under `keyAgreement` or under no relationship at all, so a key never meant for signing could sign. It also refused every `publicKeyJwk` method, so a `did:web` issuer publishing JWK keys couldn't be verified. - **Relationship check:** the method must be referenced or **embedded** under `authentication` or `assertionMethod`. `did:peer:2` profiles often list their signing key under `authentication` only, so both relationships are accepted. References may be absolute DID URLs or relative `#fragment`s. - **Key decoding:** keys are decoded with `affinidi-did-common`'s `VerificationMethod::decode_public_key`, which handles `publicKeyMultibase` and `publicKeyJwk`. It maps to the same key types as before. - **Dependency:** `affinidi-did-common` (≥ 0.4.2, for `decode_public_key`) becomes an explicit optional dependency of the `affinidi` feature. It was already in the tree through the resolver-cache SDK. ## Tests New file: `tests/raw_and_relationships.rs`. The issuer's DID document is seeded into the resolver cache, so each test states the exact document shape it's about. - `a_jwk_signing_key_verifies`: an Ed25519 `publicKeyJwk` key under `authentication` verifies. - `a_key_agreement_key_cannot_sign`: the same key under `keyAgreement` only is refused, despite a valid signature. - `the_document_as_received_verifies_where_a_reserialised_one_does_not`: a document signed with `+00:00` verifies through `verify_raw`, and fails through the typed path. This pins why `verify_raw` exists. The existing `cached_resolver`, `proof_ext` and `round_trip` suites pass unchanged. `cargo clippy -p trust-tasks-proof --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean. ## Semver - **Additive:** `verify_raw`. - **Stricter:** the resolver refuses keys outside the signing relationships. A proof made with a `keyAgreement`-only key was never a valid assertion. - No version edit, per this repo's release flow.

title: fix(proof): verify the document as received, and only keys the DID authorises for signing (#587)
body:
fix(proof): verify the document as received, and only keys the DID authorises for signing (#587) Verifier::verify_raw verifies a proof over the JSON document exactly as received. ProofVerifier::verify re-serialised the parsed TrustTask

, so any member whose serde round-trip is not byte-exact (a +00:00 timestamp re-rendered as Z) broke a genuine signature; it now delegates to verify_raw over its own serialisation. CachedDidResolver now refuses a verificationMethod that is not referenced or embedded under authentication or assertionMethod (a keyAgreement key could sign), accepts absolute or relative references, and decodes publicKeyJwk as well as publicKeyMultibase. Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore

title: fix(persona): take vta-sdk 0.48, and keep a binding's end and an attribute's endorsements through an edit
body:
vta-sdk 0.48 (verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1628, #1635, #1639) adds
binding `until`, face `reach`, profile/list `includeRetired`, attribute
`endorsements` and `derived` provenance, and the SDK calls take them.
Two of those are members an edit here would otherwise have lost, because
the writes replace the record:

- binding/set: a face change already read the binding's `label` and sent
  it back; it now does the same for `until`, so a face worn "until
  Sunday" and changed here does not become permanent. BindingSummary
  carries `until`.
- attribute/put: endorsements are read with the attribute and carried
  through the edit form into the draft, so fixing a label does not lose a
  vouch. PoolAttribute, AttributeForm and AttributeDraft gain them.

`derived` provenance is its own ProvenanceKind — "from a source you
connected" — and, like a credential-backed value, is not editable here:
rewriting it would make it self-asserted by an edit the holder did not
mean as one. It links as a typed value does. Previously it parsed as
credential-backed (the safe reading of an unknown kind) and was labelled
"credential".

profile/put sends `reach: None`, which keeps the stored reach;
profile/list asks for retired faces not to be included.

Takes vta-service 0.38.0 as the dev floor so the dev graph holds one
vta-sdk.



Verified locally with the CI set: fmt, both clippy runs, docs, `cargo test --workspace -- --include-ignored` (1489), `--no-default-features` (1470), `-p openvtc --features dev-overrides` (663), bench build.

title: fix(auth)!: a signed REST sign-in must be addressed to the service that receives it
body:
Fixes #1638.

Neither the VTA nor the VTC checked the `recipient` of a proof-signed REST `auth/authenticate/0.1` document, so a holder's signed sign-in was accepted by **whichever service received it**.

**The relay:** a malicious service A asks service B for a challenge bound to the victim, and has the victim sign an authenticate document addressed to A. A forwards the document to B, and B issues A a session **as the victim**. SPEC §7.2 item 5 and §4.8 require the check this PR adds.

## Fix

`vti_common::auth::AuthenticateInput` gains a **required** `audience: AudienceBinding` (`#[non_exhaustive]`). `handle_authenticate` checks it **first, before loading the session**, so a document addressed elsewhere learns nothing about who is enrolled.

| Binding | Used by | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `Transport` | DIDComm/TSP authcrypt, SIOP `id_token` (the route has already checked `aud`), WebAuthn passkey | The transport or credential binds the audience |
| `Recipient { recipient, own_did }` | Proof-signed REST documents | `recipient` must equal this service's own DID exactly |

Failures:
- a missing `recipient` is `malformedRequest` (400);
- another service's DID is `wrongRecipient` (401);
- a service with no DID of its own can't be addressed at all.

The field is **required** rather than optional so that every sign-in path has to state its binding, and a future one can't forget. That makes this **breaking for `vti-common`**. Downstream constructors (did-hosting's sign-in routes) will have to choose a binding on upgrade; see below.

## No lockout: every client was checked first

- `vta-sdk` `auth_di::sign_authenticate_doc` sets `recipient` to the service DID for every caller: the session store, `auth_light`, `VtcClient::connect`, `auth_rest`, `auto_connect`, `integration::auth`, and the VTC setup wizard.
- `vta-mobile-core` `build_authenticate`: `envelope_doc` sets `recipient = env.vta_did`.
- pnm-browser-plugin: `vta/auth-tasks.ts` sets `recipient: params.service.did`, and `rp-login` goes through it.
- Keyring's reference clients (`keyring-wallet/tsp-reference`) set `recipient` correctly.
- SIOP logins (`siop/login-client.ts`, the admin console's wallet login) carry an `id_token` and are bound by its `aud`, so they're unaffected.

## The tests had the bug too

The tests for this path signed to placeholder DIDs, `did:key:z6MkVtcUnderTest` and `did:key:z6MkTestVta`, which were never the service's own. The check refused them on first run, as it should. They now address the test service's real DID. That includes two tests #1643 added while this was in flight.

## Related: did-hosting (affinidi/affinidi-webvh-service#207)

`did-hosting-server` and `webvh-witness` sign in with **JWS-signed** DIDComm messages (`unpack_signed`) and never check the message's `to`. So the same relay works against both today, whatever `vti-common` version they pin. When they pick up this change, those sites must use `AudienceBinding::Recipient` with the message's `to`, **not** `Transport`, because a signature alone binds no audience. `did-hosting-control`'s Trust Task arm is already covered by `trust_tasks_rs::consume_inbound`.

## Tests

- VTA and VTC: a document addressed to another service is refused as `wrongRecipient`, and **the session survives**, so the holder can still sign in with a correctly addressed document. A document with no recipient is `malformedRequest`.
- `vti-common` unit tests for `AudienceBinding::check`: accept, mismatch, missing, exact equality with no normalisation, and a service with no DID.
- Workspace suite 4758 passed / 0 failed; vtc-service + vtc-client 1783 / 0; clippy `-D warnings` and fmt pass. After rebasing onto main I re-ran the auth suites, which is how I caught #1643's two placeholder tests.

title: REST auth/authenticate accepts a document addressed to another service (recipient not enforced, SPEC §7.2 item 5)
body:
## Summary

Neither the VTA nor the VTC checks the `recipient` of a DI-signed REST `auth/authenticate/0.1` document. A holder's signed authenticate document is accepted by whichever service receives it, not only the one it names. So the REST sign-in path has no server-side audience binding.

## What the specification requires

- **SPEC §7.2, Consumer Requirements item 5:** "Reject any document whose `recipient` member is set and does not identify the *consumer*'s own party. Where the *Trust Task specification* declares `recipient` as **REQUIRED** … reject any document lacking an in-band `recipient` with `malformedRequest`."
- **SPEC §4.8:** a document carrying a `proof` MUST carry an in-band `recipient` unless its specification is a bearer specification. `auth/authenticate` is not one.
- **`auth/authenticate/0.1` front matter:** Parties → Auth service, `requirement: REQUIRED`, `member: recipient`. The producer MUST emit "the auth service as `recipient`".

So a missing `recipient` must be refused with `malformedRequest`, and a `recipient` that is not this service's own DID must be refused too. VID comparison is exact string equality (SPEC §4.8, no normalisation).

## Where it is missing

- **VTA:** `vta-service/src/routes/auth.rs` → `try_authenticate_trust_task` checks the `type`, calls `verify_authenticate_proof` (the proof only), parses the payload, and goes straight to `vti_common::auth::handlers::handle_authenticate`. `doc.recipient` is never read.
- **VTC:** `vtc-service/src/routes/auth.rs`, the DI-signed Trust Task path (~L338: `verify_trust_task_proof_with` then `handle_authenticate`), has the same shape.
- `vti_common::auth::handlers::handle_authenticate` (`vti-common/src/auth/handlers/authenticate.rs`) receives `AuthenticateInput { session_id, challenge, signer_did, … }` with no recipient field, so the canonical handler cannot enforce it either.

These routes parse the document themselves rather than going through the Trust Task spine, so any recipient enforcement the spine performs does not apply to them.

## Impact

The single-use, TTL'd challenge limits this but does not close it.
- **The relay:** a malicious or compromised service A asks service B for a challenge bound to the victim's DID and hands it to the victim as its own. The victim signs an authenticate document naming A as `recipient`. A forwards it to B, and B issues A a session **as the victim**.
- **What would stop it:** a recipient check at B refuses the document. That is the reason the member exists.

This is the server-side half of the audience problem fixed client-side in #1637, where `cnm` was sending VTA-audience sign-ins to a VTC. The DIDComm path is unaffected: its envelope is encrypted to the recipient, so only the intended service can open it.

## Suggested fix

1. Give the check one home. Either add the expected audience to `AuthenticateInput` (the service's own DID) and have `handle_authenticate` compare it with the document's `recipient`, or add a shared `vti_common::auth` helper that both routes call before `handle_authenticate`. The first is harder to forget on a future third path.
2. Missing `recipient` → `malformedRequest`. Mismatch → refused (the spec's §7.2 item 5 failure), never a generic 500.
3. Check whether `auth/refresh/0.1` and `auth/challenge/0.1` (when sent as Trust Task documents) need the same treatment. Refresh is proofless (a bearer credential), so §4.8 may not apply; decide explicitly and record it.
4. Tests on both services:
   - `recipient` = own DID → ok.
   - Another service's DID → refused.
   - Absent → `malformedRequest`.
   - The relay scenario above, with two services → refused.
5. Clients: confirm `vta_sdk::auth_di`, `vtc-client::auth_light`, `vta-mobile-core::build_authenticate` and the TS/plugin clients all set `recipient` to the service DID, so the new check doesn't lock them out. Any that don't must be fixed first, or the change is a lockout.

## Found by

The #1637 work on `cnm` VTC sign-in.

title: vtc: tasks that declare proof REQUIRED are served on a bearer token, and the dispatcher does not enforce the requirement (VTI-OPS-020/021/024/093)
body:
Tracks the intended resolution of two divergences recorded in the VTI specification's divergence register (Appendix F.2) by trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#35. It follows from #1631, which bound `vtc/members/credentials/0.1` this way and noted that the other admin members routes do the same.

## 1. REST-only, bearer-token routes for tasks that require a proof

`vtc-service` binds 47 tasks whose front matter in dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf declares `proofRequirement: REQUIRED`. It serves them only as REST routes: the body is a flat payload, the task URI is checked against the `Trust-Task` header (`routes/mod.rs` `tt()`/`ttl()`), and the caller is authenticated by `AdminAuth` / `SuperAdminAuth` / `ManageAuth` / `AuthClaims`. No document proof is verified. `issuedAt` does not exist, although the definitions declare it REQUIRED for 41 of the 47. Nothing enters the replay record.

**Community tasks (30)**
- Admin (18): `vtc/members/{credentials, update, admin-remove, purge}`, `vtc/join-requests/decide`, `vtc/admin/invites/{create, revoke}`, `vtc/community/profile/update`, `vtc/config/{export, import}`, `vtc/backup/{export, import}`, `vtc/registry/sync-jobs/{retry, discard}`, `vtc/endorsement-types/{register, delete}`, `vtc/website/{files/delete, rollback}`
- Member session (12): `vtc/members/{renew, rotate-challenge, rotate, self-remove, personhood/assert, personhood/revoke}`, `vtc/relationships/revoke`, `vtc/endorsements/{issue, revoke}`, `vtc/invitations/{issue, revoke}`, `vtc/vetting/vetters/grant`

**Canonical tasks shared with other node types (17):** `acl/{grant, change-role, revoke}`, `config/{patch, reload, restart}`, `policy/{upsert, activate}`, `audit/list`, `auth/{whoami, sessions/list, revoke-session}`, `auth/passkey/{list, enroll/start, enroll/finish, revoke/start, revoke/finish}`

**Plus:** `vtc/auth/admin-session/0.1` is unauthenticated. It takes an access token in the body and carries no proof.

The two REST routes that do verify a document proof are `auth/authenticate/0.1` and `vtc/relationships/publish/0.2`, and they are the model to follow.

## 2. The document dispatcher does not enforce `proofRequired` or `issuedAt`

`trust_tasks::dispatch_trust_task_core` verifies a proof whenever one is present. When it is absent, the dispatcher falls back to transport attribution, including for tasks that declare the proof REQUIRED: `join-requests/{submit, status, withdraw, supplement}`, `members/{self-remove, vmc, personhood/assert}` and `vetting/{revoke-statement, vetters/grant}`. `retention_policy()` is retention-only, and no acceptance window is applied to `issuedAt`. This is deliberate and documented in the code (`spine_proof_tests`), because joining over DIDComm/TSP carries no proof today.

## Intended resolution

1. Bind each task in list 1 in `DISPATCHED_URIS` / `dispatch_typed`. Accept a DI-signed Trust Task document over `POST /v1/trust-tasks` (and over messaging), with the proof verified against the issuer's authority and `issuedAt` checked against an acceptance window. Authorization is taken from the verified signer's ACL entry.
2. Keep the bearer-JWT REST route only as a **documented transitional path** with a stated removal point, and say so in the OpenAPI description of each route.
3. Make the dispatcher enforce `Payload::IS_PROOF_REQUIRED` and `IS_ISSUED_AT_REQUIRED` (SPEC §7.2 items 7 and 13, VTI-OPS-024). This needs a decision on the DIDComm/TSP join path: either the producers sign, or the task definitions change upstream. Changing a definition is a change proposal, not an entry in the divergence register. Without this step, step 1 moves the divergence instead of closing it.
4. Close the Appendix F entries when both are done.

Clients that call these routes today (at least the admin console, `cnm` and `vtc-client`) need the signed path before the bearer routes can be removed.

title: feat(join): answer what a community asks about you, through a disclosure
body:
A join manifest 0.2 may carry `requestedAttributes` (VTI #1614): claim types, each required or not, each with a purpose. The TUI now shows them before a join launches, lets the applicant pick which face answers, and shows exactly the values that face would send. Enter approves those values.

The answers leave through `persona/disclosure/preview` → `present` in the community's context, not read out of the pool, so the holder's disclosure history records what they told the community and a `release: stepUp` claim is gated as the holder asked. The preview is compared with what was approved; anything that changed in between stops the join rather than sending something the holder did not see. The answers ride the submit as `attributes` and are labelled on the page as the applicant's own statement.

- openvtc-core `persona::join_answers`: `asked`, `preview`, `present`, `attributes_from_artifact`, `shown_by`, `preview_matches`.
- The vetting book keeps what each community asks, learned from its manifest.
- `JoinPresentation` carries `attributes` into the submit document.
- New Answers page; `launch_join_sequence` parks the launch there when a community asks and nothing is approved yet. A failure to release the answers rolls back a persona minted for the join.
- Takes vta-sdk 0.47 and floors vta-service at 0.37.1 (0.37.0 is built on vta-sdk 0.46, which would put two sdks in the dev graph).

Verified locally with the CI set: fmt, both clippy runs, docs, `cargo test --workspace -- --include-ignored` (1489), `--no-default-features` (1470), `-p openvtc --features dev-overrides` (663), bench build.

title: fix(vtc): emit the error codes the join, member, vetting and relationship tasks declare
body:
Refs #1600

The error-code census (#1636) baselined 78 declared codes that nothing showed this service emitting. This PR makes the handlers for join-requests, members, personhood, vetting (grant / revoke-statement), relationships, policies/test and website emit the codes their specifications declare. Each code gets a witness test, and each is removed from the baseline.

**Baseline: 78 → 39.** (88 declared in scope, 49 witnessed.)

## How

`vtc-service/src/error.rs` gains `TaskError`, which is either `App(AppError)` or `Declared { code, error }`. It lets a handler attach the generated `…::error_codes::X.code` to the error it already had, instead of adding a refusal enum for each task:

- **REST**: the status and the `error` member are the inner `AppError`'s own. The body gains a `code` member, so a client reading the status or the message sees nothing different. The admin UI reads `body.error` / status (`lib/api.ts`), and `vtc-client` does not parse error bodies. A unit test checks that the status and the message are unchanged.
- **Trust Task**: the new `helpers::task_error_to_reject` sends the extended code instead of `taskFailed`. For `NotFound` / `Conflict` / `Gone` it keeps the `details.reason` marker, so a client that does not know the code still gets the typed `VtaError`, as `withdraw` (#1591) and `supplement` (#1593) do. `From<TaskError> for AppError` drops the code for the DIDComm problem-report path, which answers exactly as before.

Every code constant is read from `trust_tasks_rs::specs::…::error_codes::X.code`. None is written as a literal.

## Handlers changed to emit (previously flattened) vs. tested only

All 39 needed a handler change. None of them was already emitted and merely untested.

| Task | Codes | Transport |
|---|---|---|
| join-requests/decide | notFound, notPending | REST |
| join-requests/show | notFound | REST |
| join-requests/status | notFound | TT |
| join-requests/submit | presentationInvalid | TT |
| members/show, update, admin-remove, solicit-vmc | notFound | REST |
| members/purge | notFound, lastAdministrator | REST |
| members/self-remove | notMember | TT + REST (shared `remove_inner`) |
| members/renew, rotate-challenge | notMember | REST |
| members/rotate | rotationExpired, signatureInvalid | REST |
| members/vmc | all six | TT |
| members/personhood/challenge | notFound | REST + TT |
| members/personhood/assert | notFound, challengeExpired, presentationInvalid | REST + TT |
| members/personhood/revoke | notFound | REST |
| vetting/vetters/grant | notMember | REST + TT |
| vetting/revoke-statement | notMember | TT |
| relationships/list | notFound | REST |
| relationships/publish | vrcInvalid, subjectNotMember | REST |
| relationships/revoke | notFound | REST |
| policies/test | notFound, evaluationFailed | REST |
| website/files/delete | notFound | REST |
| website/generations/list, rollback | notManaged, generationNotFound | REST |

## Behaviour changes worth reviewing

- **Trust Task status 400 → 422 where a code is now extended.** The framework maps every extended code to 422 (`trust_tasks_https::status_for_code`). This hits `members/vmc` subjectMismatch / invalidCredential, which were 400 `malformedRequest`, and `status` on a foreign request. The same happened to `attributesMissing` before. Four existing tests are updated to assert the code. **No REST status changed.**
- **`join-requests/status`: a request that belongs to someone else is now `notFound`, with the same message as a missing one.** The spec says "…or it does not belong to the proof signer". Before, this answered `malformedRequest` and named the mismatch, which let any identified caller find out which request ids exist.
- **`join-requests/submit` now rejects a VP whose `holder` is not the proof signer** (`presentationInvalid`). The spec's Authorization section makes holder == signer the whole authorization. Before, `presentation_from_vp` took the VP's holder, marked it `verified: true` and decided on it. An absent holder is still read as the applicant. `supplement` gets the same check as `malformedRequest`, because its spec declares no code for it. This is a security fix, not only a code change. One unit test (`vic_bound_to_another_did_cannot_be_redeemed`) now hits this check first. It is updated, and it gains a holder-less case that still reaches the invitation's `Forbidden`.
- **`relationships/list` for a DID with neither an ACL row nor a member row is now 404 `notFound`.** It used to return an empty page. A tombstoned member still lists. The admin UI only calls this from a member's detail page, and that page already 404s for such a DID.
- **`policies/test` evaluationFailed keeps the evaluator's existing statuses:** 400 for a compile error, 500 for an evaluation error. A 500 for an operator's bad query is arguably wrong, but changing it is a status change the spec does not require. A resource-budget abort is not declared.

## Left baselined (39)

**In the families above: need a design decision**
- `join-requests/submit:policyUnsatisfied`. submit/0.2's Conformance says to return it when the VP "does not satisfy the active join policy". The same paragraph, and the response schema, answer a policy refusal as a `deny` verdict, and that is what this service returns (the status poll recovers its code and reason). Emitting both is not coherent. The spec needs to say which it means.
- `members/update:adminRoleForbidden`. The spec says promotion to admin "is a separate, gated flow, not a metadata update". This service promotes through `PATCH /members/{did}` behind a fresh passkey step-up, and the admin UI's promote flow depends on it. Emitting the code means removing that path. This belongs in the divergence register, not in this PR.
- `vetting/revoke-statement:issuerMismatch`, `:digestMismatch`. Both need the community to look up a *held* statement by id. The current design records a notice keyed by (sender, id, digest) and has no statement index: a notice about someone else's statement is stored under the wrong issuer and matches nothing. Emitting these needs an index over the vetting facts stored with each join request, plus a decision on what the refusal reveals.
- Partial, noted but not baselined: `relationships/revoke:notFound` now covers the missing row. The spec also folds "the proof signer is not its issuer" into `notFound`. That case still answers 403, because turning it into 404 is a status change and it would also hide admin moderation.

**Out of scope for this PR (not attempted)**
- `vtc/invitations/*` (2) is owned by another session (feat/vtc-invitations-deliver).

title: fix(vtc): emit the error codes the join, member, vetting and relationship tasks declare (#1644)
body:
fix(vtc): emit the error codes the join, member, vetting and relationship tasks declare (#1644)

Refs #1600. The declared-error-code census (#1636) baselined 78 codes that
nothing showed this service emitting. 39 of them are now emitted and
witnessed, so the baseline goes from 78 to 39.

Each of the 39 was flattened into the generic `AppError` rendering. The new
`crate::error::TaskError` attaches the generated `error_codes::X.code` to the
error the handler already had.

- REST keeps the inner error's status and `error` member, and adds `code`.
- The Trust Task path sends the extended code, and keeps the
  `details.reason` marker for NotFound, Conflict and Gone
  (`helpers::task_error_to_reject`).
- The DIDComm problem-report path drops the code and answers as it did
  before.

Behaviour changes:

- A Trust Task refusal that now carries an extended code is 422 rather than
  400, the framework's mapping for every extended code. No REST status
  changed.
- join-requests/status answers `notFound` for a request that belongs to
  someone else, with the same message as a missing one. It used to answer
  malformedRequest naming the mismatch, which was an id oracle.
- join-requests/submit refuses a VP whose `holder` is not the proof signer,
  as `presentationInvalid`, as submit/0.2's Authorization requires. It used
  to be decided on. supplement gets the same check as malformedRequest.
- relationships/list answers 404 `notFound` for a DID with neither an ACL
  row nor a member row, instead of an empty page.

Left baselined, each needing a design decision:

- submit:policyUnsatisfied. The spec also answers a policy refusal with a
  `deny` verdict.
- members/update:adminRoleForbidden. Promotion goes through update behind a
  step-up.
- revoke-statement:issuerMismatch and :digestMismatch. There is no index of
  held statements.

Not attempted: invitations and auth (owned elsewhere), and the admin,
backup, community, config, directory, endorsement-types, endorsements and
install families.

title: vta-service-v0.38.0
body:
### Added

- **persona**: Derived provenance, and endorsements as inventory ([#1639](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1639))

* feat(persona)!: derived provenance, and endorsements as inventory

  Implements trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#582 (design note
  docs/05-design-notes/persona-context-first.md §5.7).

- **persona**: Where a face may be worn, where it is, and what it has done ([#1635](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1635))

Implements trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#577 (design note
  docs/05-design-notes/persona-context-first.md §5.4, §9.6).

  Face reach. A pool face carries `reach` — FaceReach::Anywhere (default)
  or Only { context_ids } — an enum rather than a context list, so
  unrestricted and nowhere cannot be confused (#746/#769/#770).
  binding/set refuses a face outside its reach (`outsideReach`);
  profile/put refuses to narrow it past a context the face is worn in
  (`boundOutsideReach`, naming them). An omitted reach on profile/put keeps
  the face's current one: a client written before reach existed must not
  lift a restriction by saving an edit.

  persona/profile/usage — where a face is worn now, each binding's
  `until`, and the reach beside them.

  persona/profile/timeline — one face's history, oldest first: composed,
  worn, unworn, expired, disclosed, valueChanged, promoted, retired,
  reinstated. A binding taken off left no trace, so each face now has an
  append-only event log (`pft:`, agent-scoped, ULID-keyed so recording
  never takes the write lock), written after the change it describes and
  never failing it; the timeline joins it with the disclosure records. A
  face from before the log reports its composition from createdAt. A
  promoted face keeps its log; a deleted one loses it. FaceEvent has no
  member a value or label could go in, and a test holds that none reaches
  the wire.

  profile/compose takes `until` (`untilNotFuture`).

  `pnm persona profile usage|timeline`, `put --reach-only/--reach-anywhere`,
  `compose --until`. Takes trust-tasks-rs 0.21.14.

- **persona**: Retire a face, warn before deleting one, and let a binding end on its own ([#1628](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1628))

Implements trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#570 (design note
  docs/05-design-notes/persona-context-first.md §9.4, §9.5).

  persona/profile/retire and persona/profile/reinstate, for pool and
  context-local faces. Retire marks the face before clearing its bindings,
  so an interrupted retire leaves a face that cannot be newly worn and a
  repeat finishes the clearing; the cleared bindings come back in
  `unbound`. binding/set and local/binding/set refuse a retired face
  (`profileRetired`), profile/list leaves retired faces out unless
  `includeRetired`. Reinstate binds nothing. Profile gains `status` and
  `retiredAt`.

  Binding `until` on binding/set and local/binding/set, returned by
  binding/get and binding/list; `untilNotFuture` refuses one in the past or
  on a cleared binding. A lapsed binding reads as cleared at once — every
  binding read decodes through BindingRecord::into_read, and present
  refuses a preview whose persona no longer wears a face — whether or not
  the sweeper has run. The storage-thread sweeper (expire_bindings,
  audited as persona.binding.expire) makes the clear durable and retires a
  face the expiry left worn nowhere; never one still worn elsewhere, and
  never deletes.

  profile/get and profile/delete return `disclosedTo` {partyCount,
  contextCount}; `pnm persona profile delete` says "deleting does not
  un-tell them". Disclosure records now carry the face they were made
  through; an older record is attributed through its binding where that
  still wears the face.

  `pnm persona profile retire|reinstate`, `list --include-retired`,
  `binding set --until`, `local binding set --until`. Retire is
  Destructive for the MCP guard (it withdraws access everywhere at once),
  reinstate Mutating; both RetrySafe.

  Takes trust-tasks-rs 0.21.12.

- **persona**: Compose a face where it is asked for, and promote a local value ([#1623](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1623))

* feat(persona)!: compose a face where it is asked for, and promote a local value

  Implements persona/profile/compose/1.0 and persona/attribute/promote/1.0
  (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#569; design note
  docs/05-design-notes/persona-context-first.md §2.1, §5.3).

  compose — a face for one context, from values typed now and attributes
  already held, optionally worn there in the same act. Local by default: a
  typed value is carried inline and enters no pool unless the claim says
  `share: pool`, when a self-asserted pool attribute holding exactly that
  type and value is referenced, and created only if none exists. Where the
  face lives follows from its claims — all local makes a context-local
  face, anything pooled or held a pool face. Everything is validated before
  anything is written (unresolvedReference, duplicateSlot,
  labelWithoutPersona), and a later failure removes the attributes the
  compose created.

  promote — named entries of a context-local face become pool attributes
  and the face moves into the pool with its id, name, order, slots and
  wearers unchanged. One-way. The pool face is written and the bindings
  moved before the local face is removed, so an interrupted promote leaves
  the local face worn and a retry finishes it, reusing what it made.
  versionConflict and entryOutOfRange refuse a stale or out-of-range read.

  Both holder-only (Reach::Holder), classified Keyed for retry, Mutating
  for the MCP guard. `pnm persona profile compose` and `pnm persona
  attribute promote`. The design note records what the built form changed:
  the `profile` noun, no inline findings (analyze with `candidate` is the
  pre-write warning), no facetId, self-asserted-only reuse, and §9.7's
  DID minting left for its own design.

- **vta**: TSP is on by default, and setup checks the mediator carries it ([#1622](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1622))

Keyring VTI-33. TSP is the preferred transport across the stack, but a
  default VTA build could not receive it. `tsp` joins vta-service's and
  vta-enclave's default features; the setup wizard pre-ticks TSP, and a setup
  file enables it unless it says `tsp = false` — including a `[services]`
  block given without a `tsp` key, which gets its own deserializer so the
  runtime `ServicesConfig` can keep its `false` default (a hand-written config
  that never mentions TSP must not start claiming it).

  On-by-default is only safe if the mediator `#tsp` names routes TSP, so setup
  now checks: a mediator it creates is created with `#tsp`; an existing one is
  resolved and its DID document read for a `TSPTransport` service (by type).
  Without one the wizard drops TSP and says so, and `--from` refuses, both
  before anything is minted. An unresolvable mediator gets a warning.

  Existing VTAs are unchanged; `pnm services tsp enable` adds TSP. CI's
  `tsp transport` step duplicated the default build and now builds without
  `tsp` instead.

  Behaviour change: a `--from` file whose existing mediator advertises no
  `TSPTransport` now fails setup unless it sets `services.tsp = false`.

- **acl**: `key-export` is its own capability, and minting a DID needs `KeyMint`, not admin ([#1619](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1619))

Keyring finding VTI-23: `webvh/dids/create` and `keys/export-secret` both checked
  for the admin role, so a least-privilege manager was impossible for the persona
  lifecycle — an `initiator` holds `KeyMint` and `Sign` and was refused both.

title: vta-policy-v0.3.18
body:
### Fixed

- **vta**: Warn at boot when approval rules exist but policy enforcement is off ([#1633](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1633))

Keyring KR-22 (Refs #1608). `policy.enforcement` defaults to false and stays
  that way: flipping it would turn every written-but-not-intended policy into a
  gate across existing deployments on upgrade. The defect was the silence — a
  rule written with `pnm approvals require` is stored, listed and explained, and
  then gates nothing, with no signal anywhere that enforcement is off.

  - vta-policy: `unenforced_policies()` (+ `#[non_exhaustive]`
    `UnenforcedPolicies`) reports the approval rules on the enabled declarative
    row and the ids of enabled hand-authored rows. The boot-installed baseline,
    disabled rows and a declarative row carrying only approver sets are not
    counted — none would gate a task with enforcement on.
  - vta-service: on boot with enforcement off, log a WARN naming what is being
    ignored and the exact change (`[policy] enforcement = true` + restart).
    Advisory only: a failure to read the rows is logged and never stops boot.
    The enforcement flag is copied out so the config lock is not held across
    the keyspace read.
  - docs/02-vta/approvals.md: state up front that approvals are opt-in and off
    by default, show the config snippet, and document the boot warning.

title: vti-secrets-v0.4.0
body:
### Fixed

- **vta**: Contexts/secrets requires KeyExport (VTI-VTA-003) ([#1634](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1634))

`vta/contexts/secrets/1.0` (`get_context_secrets`) released a context DID's
  private keys to any `Application`-role caller in that context. Its only gate
  was the role floor (`require_write`, which also admits `Initiator`) plus the
  context scope. VTI-VTA-003 says an export of derived key material "MUST be
  gated by a capability distinct from the capability to use the key, and MUST
  be audited". The audit was already there; the separate capability was not.
  An `Application` can *use* its context's keys through the signing oracle, and
  under the old gate that also let it *take* them. That is the case the
  requirement exists for: keys that were taken stay with the caller after its
  authority is withdrawn.

title: pnm-cli-v0.20.0
body:
### Added

- **pnm**: Name the console's accounts from the VTA ([#1640](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1640))

The mediator console shows accounts as sha256(did) hashes. Fill its
  address book (mediator-console 0.1.2) with every DID this VTA can name,
  least to most specific: ACL entries by label, hosted webvh DIDs as
  'context · mnemonic', this session's context DIDs by context name, the
  VTA and the pnm session. The names are supplied, not saved; names the
  user adds in the console are saved to the shared address book and win.
  A source this session may not read is skipped.
