title: cnm-cli-v0.17.1
body:
### Added

- **vtc**: A self-hosted community installs its own DID log over did-management/did/register ([#1632](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1632))

Keyring VTI-35. A community whose DID is `did:webvh:<scid>:<host>` serves
  its own did.jsonl, but the VTA holds the keys that extend it and cannot
  reach the community's copy, and the VTC keeps no VTA credential after
  setup. So an entry the VTA appends later — a TSP transport added to the
  community's services, a key rotated — had no way to the community except
  an operator copying the file by hand. (A community on a DID host needs
  none of this: the VTA publishes each entry to the host itself.)

  The VTC now answers `did-management/did/register/0.1` — the task a DID
  owner sends a DID host, where a second register with a longer log is an
  update — for its own DID at the root slot `.well-known`, over
  `POST /v1/admin/did/register` (super-admin). Before serving, it verifies
  the whole log (every entry's proof under the update keys in force, SCID,
  hash chain), that it is the community's own DID, and that every served
  entry survives unchanged as a prefix; then swaps the file atomically,
  with no restart. So an administrator's authority covers delivery only: a
  log the key holder did not sign, or one that moves the served log
  backwards, is refused whoever delivers it. The prefix rule is stricter
  than `register` alone and carries a consumer-minted code (SPEC §8.5).

  - `cnm did-log install --file did.jsonl`, fed by `pnm did-mgmt dids
    get-log`. It authenticates to the community directly, with the
    community's DID as the audience (`VtcClient::connect`), not through the
    profile's VTA session, whose audience is the VTA's DID — a VTC refuses
    that. The community DID comes from the log; the URL from its host.
  - `VtcClient::install_did_log`; `MockVtc::start_with` for a test VTC with
    a self-hosted DID; a live test authenticates and installs over HTTP.
  - AuditEvent::CommunityDidLogInstalled.
  - The redeploy hint for a DID the VTA manages but does not serve names
    the new command.



### Fixed

- **cnm**: Vetting, audit and backup authenticate to a VTC with its own DID as audience ([#1637](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1637))

`cnm vetting`, `cnm audit verify` and `cnm backup` could not sign in to a
  VTC. All three took a token from `SessionStore::ensure_authenticated`, whose
  audience is not a parameter: it is always the session's bound *VTA* DID, and
  the DIDComm authenticate envelope it builds is encrypted to that DID's
  key-agreement key. A VTC holds only its own keys, cannot open the envelope,
  and refuses the login. `cnm vetting` then also built its `VtcClient` with the
  VTA's DID as the community's DID. main connected to the VTA first, so without
  `--url` the requests went to the VTA's REST URL too.

  They now authenticate the way `cnm did-log install` does ([#1632](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1632)):
  `VtcClient::connect(base, vtc_did, client_did, key)` with the profile's DID
  and key, and the VTC's DID as the audience. They are exempt from
  `requires_auth`, so no VTA connection is made first.

  Where the VTC's DID comes from: `--vtc-did` (env `CNM_VTC_DID`), else a new
  optional `vtc_did` on the community profile, set with
  `cnm community set-vtc <did>`. The DID is never read from the server (for
  example the VTC's `/health`): it is the audience the sign-in is signed for,
  and a server allowed to name it could name another community's DID and
  relay the signed document there. Discovery runs from DID to URL, as it does
  for a VTA: `--url` if given, otherwise the `VTCRest` service in the DID's
  document, matched on `type` and checked by the same endpoint guard as a
  VTA's advertised REST URL.

  The root cause is a generic "token for this base URL" helper sitting on a
  session bound to one audience. `cnm`'s `auth::ensure_authenticated` wrapper
  is removed, so nothing in `cnm` can reach the VTC through the VTA session
  again, and `SessionStore::ensure_authenticated` now documents that it
  authenticates to the session's VTA only. Nothing else in the workspace
  used `SessionStore` against a VTC.

  When the VTC refuses the sign-in, `cnm` prints the fix with the DID filled
  in: `vtc --config <config.toml> acl add --did <DID> --role admin --label cnm`,
  or Access control, Add entry in the console. A VTC answers every
  authentication failure the same way (VTI-SES-007), so the message names the
  usual cause rather than claiming it.

  Routing these through a live VTC exposed two more faults on the same paths,
  fixed here:
  - `cnm backup export` saved the `{ envelope }` response (the export shape
    since #1059) instead of the envelope, so the file printed `(none)` for
    its source DID and could not be imported. `VtcClient::export_backup`
    returns the envelope, and accepts a pre-#1059 bare one.
  - `cnm audit verify` read the signed-checkpoint result from the top level,
    but #1110 moved it under `ext["org.openvtc"]`. Every report therefore
    looked like it had no checkpoint result, and a truncated log that the
    community key contradicts passed as long as its hash chain did. It reads
    both places now, and fails on any checkpoint status it does not know
    rather than passing it.

  `REST_SERVICE_TYPE` and `api_base_from_did_document`, plus the three task

* feat(persona)!: derived provenance, and endorsements as inventory

  Implements trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#582 (design note
  docs/05-design-notes/persona-context-first.md §5.7).

- **persona**: Where a face may be worn, where it is, and what it has done ([#1635](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1635))

Implements trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#577 (design note
  docs/05-design-notes/persona-context-first.md §5.4, §9.6).

  Face reach. A pool face carries `reach` — FaceReach::Anywhere (default)
  or Only { context_ids } — an enum rather than a context list, so
  unrestricted and nowhere cannot be confused (#746/#769/#770).
  binding/set refuses a face outside its reach (`outsideReach`);
  profile/put refuses to narrow it past a context the face is worn in
  (`boundOutsideReach`, naming them). An omitted reach on profile/put keeps
  the face's current one: a client written before reach existed must not
  lift a restriction by saving an edit.

  persona/profile/usage — where a face is worn now, each binding's
  `until`, and the reach beside them.

  persona/profile/timeline — one face's history, oldest first: composed,
  worn, unworn, expired, disclosed, valueChanged, promoted, retired,
  reinstated. A binding taken off left no trace, so each face now has an
  append-only event log (`pft:`, agent-scoped, ULID-keyed so recording
  never takes the write lock), written after the change it describes and
  never failing it; the timeline joins it with the disclosure records. A
  face from before the log reports its composition from createdAt. A
  promoted face keeps its log; a deleted one loses it. FaceEvent has no
  member a value or label could go in, and a test holds that none reaches
  the wire.

  profile/compose takes `until` (`untilNotFuture`).

  `pnm persona profile usage|timeline`, `put --reach-only/--reach-anywhere`,
  `compose --until`. Takes trust-tasks-rs 0.21.14.

  reach the community's copy, and the VTC keeps no VTA credential after
  setup. So an entry the VTA appends later — a TSP transport added to the
  community's services, a key rotated — had no way to the community except
  an operator copying the file by hand. (A community on a DID host needs
  none of this: the VTA publishes each entry to the host itself.)

  owner sends a DID host, where a second register with a longer log is an
  update — for its own DID at the root slot `.well-known`, over

  the whole log (every entry's proof under the update keys in force, SCID,
  hash chain), that it is the community's own DID, and that every served
  entry survives unchanged as a prefix; then swaps the file atomically,
  with no restart. So an administrator's authority covers delivery only: a
  log the key holder did not sign, or one that moves the served log
  backwards, is refused whoever delivers it. The prefix rule is stricter
  than `register` alone and carries a consumer-minted code (SPEC §8.5).

  - `cnm did-log install --file did.jsonl`, fed by `pnm did-mgmt dids
    get-log`. It authenticates to the community directly, with the
    community's DID as the audience (`VtcClient::connect`), not through the
    profile's VTA session, whose audience is the VTA's DID — a VTC refuses
    that. The community DID comes from the log; the URL from its host.
  - `VtcClient::install_did_log`; `MockVtc::start_with` for a test VTC with
    a self-hosted DID; a live test authenticates and installs over HTTP.
  - AuditEvent::CommunityDidLogInstalled.
  - The redeploy hint for a DID the VTA manages but does not serve names
    the new command.

- **persona**: Retire a face, warn before deleting one, and let a binding end on its own ([#1628](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1628))

Implements trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#570 (design note
  docs/05-design-notes/persona-context-first.md §9.4, §9.5).

  persona/profile/retire and persona/profile/reinstate, for pool and
  context-local faces. Retire marks the face before clearing its bindings,
  so an interrupted retire leaves a face that cannot be newly worn and a
  repeat finishes the clearing; the cleared bindings come back in
  `unbound`. binding/set and local/binding/set refuse a retired face
  (`profileRetired`), profile/list leaves retired faces out unless
  `includeRetired`. Reinstate binds nothing. Profile gains `status` and
  `retiredAt`.

  Binding `until` on binding/set and local/binding/set, returned by
  binding/get and binding/list; `untilNotFuture` refuses one in the past or
  on a cleared binding. A lapsed binding reads as cleared at once — every
  binding read decodes through BindingRecord::into_read, and present
  refuses a preview whose persona no longer wears a face — whether or not
  the sweeper has run. The storage-thread sweeper (expire_bindings,
  audited as persona.binding.expire) makes the clear durable and retires a
  face the expiry left worn nowhere; never one still worn elsewhere, and
  never deletes.

  contextCount}; `pnm persona profile delete` says "deleting does not
  un-tell them". Disclosure records now carry the face they were made
  through; an older record is attributed through its binding where that
  still wears the face.

  `binding set --until`, `local binding set --until`. Retire is
  Destructive for the MCP guard (it withdraws access everywhere at once),
  reinstate Mutating; both RetrySafe.

* feat(persona)!: compose a face where it is asked for, and promote a local value

  Implements persona/profile/compose/1.0 and persona/attribute/promote/1.0
  (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#569; design note
  docs/05-design-notes/persona-context-first.md §2.1, §5.3).

  compose — a face for one context, from values typed now and attributes
  already held, optionally worn there in the same act. Local by default: a
  typed value is carried inline and enters no pool unless the claim says
  `share: pool`, when a self-asserted pool attribute holding exactly that
  type and value is referenced, and created only if none exists. Where the
  face lives follows from its claims — all local makes a context-local
  face, anything pooled or held a pool face. Everything is validated before
  anything is written (unresolvedReference, duplicateSlot,
  labelWithoutPersona), and a later failure removes the attributes the
  compose created.

  and the face moves into the pool with its id, name, order, slots and
  wearers unchanged. One-way. The pool face is written and the bindings
  moved before the local face is removed, so an interrupted promote leaves
  the local face worn and a retry finishes it, reusing what it made.
  versionConflict and entryOutOfRange refuse a stale or out-of-range read.

  for the MCP guard. `pnm persona profile compose` and `pnm persona
  attribute promote`. The design note records what the built form changed:
  the `profile` noun, no inline findings (analyze with `candidate` is the
  pre-write warning), no facetId, self-asserted-only reuse, and §9.7's
  DID minting left for its own design.



### Fixed

- **cli**: A self-hosted VTA is not told to redeploy the log it serves ([#1624](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1624))

Keyring VTI-36. After a service mutation on a self-hosted ("serverless")
  VTA, the CLI said to fetch the log and "redeploy did.jsonl to your host".
  But the VTA serves its own did.jsonl from its store at the DID's canonical
  path, read per request, so the new entry is already published — the host
  the operator was told to redeploy to is the VTA. The hint now says so,
  names the URL, and notes the resolver cache window; only a copy published
  elsewhere needs replacing. The offline `vta services` surface says the
  entry is served once the daemon starts.

  `dids edit` on a self-hosted DID the VTA manages for someone else (a
  community's) still gets the redeploy advice, which is right there, now
  without calling it "this VTA's DID".

    the new command.

- **vtc**: Serve a member's credential bodies and show them in the admin console ([#1631](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1631))

`GET /v1/members/{did}/credentials`, bound to the now-published
  `vtc/members/credentials/0.1` (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#336,
  already in the locked trust-tasks-rs 0.21.11). AdminAuth. It reads the
  four fields #1213 keeps on the member row (`current_vmc`,
  `current_role_vec`, `member_vmc`, `member_vmc_bound`): no new storage and
  no new verification. `memberVmcBound` is the answer recorded at receipt,
  never recomputed.

  type, documented through a new `vta_sdk::openapi::MemberCredentials01Response`
  wrapper. Bodies are carried as stored. `memberVmcReceivedAt` is only sent
  alongside `memberVmc`, because the spec says a maintainer MUST NOT send one
  without the other, and a row from before #1213 has the receipt time but no
  body.

  `vtc/members/credentials:notFound`, next to the usual `error` member.
  "Unknown" means what it means for `members/show`: no member row, or no ACL
  row, so a tombstoned member counts. A member who holds nothing gets a 200
  with every document absent and `memberVmcBound: false`, as the spec
  requires.

  The spec says a maintainer SHOULD record that the read happened, so every
  successful read writes a new `MemberCredentialsRead` audit event. The event
  names which documents were disclosed and never includes their contents.
  The audit write happens before the response. `AuditEvent` is
  `#[non_exhaustive]`, so the new variant does not break any consumer.

  A conformance witness checks the task. It builds its response with the
  handler's own `credentials_response`, over a row filled by the real
  `record_issued_credentials` / `record_member_vmc`, so it tests what the
  service sends rather than a hand-typed fixture.

Keyring finding VTI-23: `webvh/dids/create` and `keys/export-secret` both checked
  for the admin role, so a least-privilege manager was impossible for the persona
  lifecycle — an `initiator` holds `KeyMint` and `Sign` and was refused both.

  the face's current one: a client written before reach existed must not
  lift a restriction by saving an edit.

  persona/profile/usage — where a face is worn now, each binding's
  `until`, and the reach beside them.

  persona/profile/timeline — one face's history, oldest first: composed,
  worn, unworn, expired, disclosed, valueChanged, promoted, retired,
  reinstated. A binding taken off left no trace, so each face now has an
  append-only event log (`pft:`, agent-scoped, ULID-keyed so recording
  never takes the write lock), written after the change it describes and
  never failing it; the timeline joins it with the disclosure records. A
  face from before the log reports its composition from createdAt. A
  promoted face keeps its log; a deleted one loses it. FaceEvent has no
  member a value or label could go in, and a test holds that none reaches
  the wire.

  profile/compose takes `until` (`untilNotFuture`).

  `pnm persona profile usage|timeline`, `put --reach-only/--reach-anywhere`,
  `compose --until`. Takes trust-tasks-rs 0.21.14.

- **vtc**: A self-hosted community installs its own DID log over did-management/did/register ([#1632](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1632))

Keyring VTI-35. A community whose DID is `did:webvh:<scid>:<host>` serves
  its own did.jsonl, but the VTA holds the keys that extend it and cannot
  reach the community's copy, and the VTC keeps no VTA credential after
  setup. So an entry the VTA appends later — a TSP transport added to the
  community's services, a key rotated — had no way to the community except
  an operator copying the file by hand. (A community on a DID host needs
  none of this: the VTA publishes each entry to the host itself.)

  The VTC now answers `did-management/did/register/0.1` — the task a DID
  owner sends a DID host, where a second register with a longer log is an
  update — for its own DID at the root slot `.well-known`, over
  `POST /v1/admin/did/register` (super-admin). Before serving, it verifies
  the whole log (every entry's proof under the update keys in force, SCID,
  hash chain), that it is the community's own DID, and that every served
  entry survives unchanged as a prefix; then swaps the file atomically,
  with no restart. So an administrator's authority covers delivery only: a
  log the key holder did not sign, or one that moves the served log
  backwards, is refused whoever delivers it. The prefix rule is stricter
  than `register` alone and carries a consumer-minted code (SPEC §8.5).

  - `cnm did-log install --file did.jsonl`, fed by `pnm did-mgmt dids
    get-log`. It authenticates to the community directly, with the
    community's DID as the audience (`VtcClient::connect`), not through the
    profile's VTA session, whose audience is the VTA's DID — a VTC refuses
    that. The community DID comes from the log; the URL from its host.
  - `VtcClient::install_did_log`; `MockVtc::start_with` for a test VTC with
    a self-hosted DID; a live test authenticates and installs over HTTP.
  - AuditEvent::CommunityDidLogInstalled.
  - The redeploy hint for a DID the VTA manages but does not serve names
    the new command.

- **vtc**: Serve a member's credential bodies and show them in the admin console ([#1631](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1631))

`GET /v1/members/{did}/credentials`, bound to the now-published
  `vtc/members/credentials/0.1` (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#336,
  already in the locked trust-tasks-rs 0.21.11). AdminAuth. It reads the
  four fields #1213 keeps on the member row (`current_vmc`,
  `current_role_vec`, `member_vmc`, `member_vmc_bound`): no new storage and
  no new verification. `memberVmcBound` is the answer recorded at receipt,
  never recomputed.

  The response is the generated `specs::vtc::members::credentials::v0_1`
  type, documented through a new `vta_sdk::openapi::MemberCredentials01Response`
  wrapper. Bodies are carried as stored. `memberVmcReceivedAt` is only sent
  alongside `memberVmc`, because the spec says a maintainer MUST NOT send one
  without the other, and a row from before #1213 has the receipt time but no
  body.

  An unknown member gets a 404 whose body carries the spec's declared code,
  `vtc/members/credentials:notFound`, next to the usual `error` member.
  "Unknown" means what it means for `members/show`: no member row, or no ACL
  row, so a tombstoned member counts. A member who holds nothing gets a 200
  with every document absent and `memberVmcBound: false`, as the spec
  requires.

  The spec says a maintainer SHOULD record that the read happened, so every
  successful read writes a new `MemberCredentialsRead` audit event. The event
  names which documents were disclosed and never includes their contents.
  The audit write happens before the response. `AuditEvent` is
  `#[non_exhaustive]`, so the new variant does not break any consumer.

  A conformance witness checks the task. It builds its response with the
  handler's own `credentials_response`, over a row filled by the real
  `record_issued_credentials` / `record_member_vmc`, so it tests what the
  service sends rather than a hand-typed fixture.

- **persona**: Retire a face, warn before deleting one, and let a binding end on its own ([#1628](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1628))

Implements trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#570 (design note
  docs/05-design-notes/persona-context-first.md §9.4, §9.5).

  persona/profile/retire and persona/profile/reinstate, for pool and
  context-local faces. Retire marks the face before clearing its bindings,
  so an interrupted retire leaves a face that cannot be newly worn and a
  repeat finishes the clearing; the cleared bindings come back in
  `unbound`. binding/set and local/binding/set refuse a retired face
  (`profileRetired`), profile/list leaves retired faces out unless
  `includeRetired`. Reinstate binds nothing. Profile gains `status` and
  `retiredAt`.

  Binding `until` on binding/set and local/binding/set, returned by
  binding/get and binding/list; `untilNotFuture` refuses one in the past or
  on a cleared binding. A lapsed binding reads as cleared at once — every
  binding read decodes through BindingRecord::into_read, and present
  refuses a preview whose persona no longer wears a face — whether or not
  the sweeper has run. The storage-thread sweeper (expire_bindings,
  audited as persona.binding.expire) makes the clear durable and retires a
  face the expiry left worn nowhere; never one still worn elsewhere, and
  never deletes.

  profile/get and profile/delete return `disclosedTo` {partyCount,
  contextCount}; `pnm persona profile delete` says "deleting does not
  un-tell them". Disclosure records now carry the face they were made
  through; an older record is attributed through its binding where that
  still wears the face.

  `pnm persona profile retire|reinstate`, `list --include-retired`,
  `binding set --until`, `local binding set --until`. Retire is
  Destructive for the MCP guard (it withdraws access everywhere at once),
  reinstate Mutating; both RetrySafe.

  Takes trust-tasks-rs 0.21.12.

- **persona**: Compose a face where it is asked for, and promote a local value ([#1623](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1623))

* feat(persona)!: compose a face where it is asked for, and promote a local value

  Implements persona/profile/compose/1.0 and persona/attribute/promote/1.0
  (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#569; design note
  docs/05-design-notes/persona-context-first.md §2.1, §5.3).

  compose — a face for one context, from values typed now and attributes
  already held, optionally worn there in the same act. Local by default: a
  typed value is carried inline and enters no pool unless the claim says
  `share: pool`, when a self-asserted pool attribute holding exactly that
  type and value is referenced, and created only if none exists. Where the
  face lives follows from its claims — all local makes a context-local
  face, anything pooled or held a pool face. Everything is validated before
  anything is written (unresolvedReference, duplicateSlot,
  labelWithoutPersona), and a later failure removes the attributes the
  compose created.

  promote — named entries of a context-local face become pool attributes
  and the face moves into the pool with its id, name, order, slots and
  wearers unchanged. One-way. The pool face is written and the bindings
  moved before the local face is removed, so an interrupted promote leaves
  the local face worn and a retry finishes it, reusing what it made.
  versionConflict and entryOutOfRange refuse a stale or out-of-range read.

  Both holder-only (Reach::Holder), classified Keyed for retry, Mutating
  for the MCP guard. `pnm persona profile compose` and `pnm persona
  attribute promote`. The design note records what the built form changed:
  the `profile` noun, no inline findings (analyze with `candidate` is the
  pre-write warning), no facetId, self-asserted-only reuse, and §9.7's
  DID minting left for its own design.



### Fixed

- **cnm**: Vetting, audit and backup authenticate to a VTC with its own DID as audience ([#1637](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1637))

`cnm vetting`, `cnm audit verify` and `cnm backup` could not sign in to a
  VTC. All three took a token from `SessionStore::ensure_authenticated`, whose
  audience is not a parameter: it is always the session's bound *VTA* DID, and
  the DIDComm authenticate envelope it builds is encrypted to that DID's
  key-agreement key. A VTC holds only its own keys, cannot open the envelope,
  and refuses the login. `cnm vetting` then also built its `VtcClient` with the
  VTA's DID as the community's DID. main connected to the VTA first, so without
  `--url` the requests went to the VTA's REST URL too.

  They now authenticate the way `cnm did-log install` does ([#1632](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1632)):
  `VtcClient::connect(base, vtc_did, client_did, key)` with the profile's DID
  and key, and the VTC's DID as the audience. They are exempt from
  `requires_auth`, so no VTA connection is made first.

  Where the VTC's DID comes from: `--vtc-did` (env `CNM_VTC_DID`), else a new
  optional `vtc_did` on the community profile, set with
  `cnm community set-vtc <did>`. The DID is never read from the server (for
  example the VTC's `/health`): it is the audience the sign-in is signed for,
  and a server allowed to name it could name another community's DID and
  relay the signed document there. Discovery runs from DID to URL, as it does
  for a VTA: `--url` if given, otherwise the `VTCRest` service in the DID's
  document, matched on `type` and checked by the same endpoint guard as a
  VTA's advertised REST URL.

  The root cause is a generic "token for this base URL" helper sitting on a
  session bound to one audience. `cnm`'s `auth::ensure_authenticated` wrapper
  is removed, so nothing in `cnm` can reach the VTC through the VTA session
  again, and `SessionStore::ensure_authenticated` now documents that it
  authenticates to the session's VTA only. Nothing else in the workspace
  used `SessionStore` against a VTC.

  When the VTC refuses the sign-in, `cnm` prints the fix with the DID filled
  in: `vtc --config <config.toml> acl add --did <DID> --role admin --label cnm`,
  or Access control, Add entry in the console. A VTC answers every
  authentication failure the same way (VTI-SES-007), so the message names the
  usual cause rather than claiming it.

  Routing these through a live VTC exposed two more faults on the same paths,
  fixed here:
  - `cnm backup export` saved the `{ envelope }` response (the export shape
    since #1059) instead of the envelope, so the file printed `(none)` for
    its source DID and could not be imported. `VtcClient::export_backup`
    returns the envelope, and accepts a pre-#1059 bare one.
  - `cnm audit verify` read the signed-checkpoint result from the top level,
    but #1110 moved it under `ext["org.openvtc"]`. Every report therefore
    looked like it had no checkpoint result, and a truncated log that the
    community key contradicts passed as long as its hash chain did. It reads
    both places now, and fails on any checkpoint status it does not know
    rather than passing it.

  vtc-client gains `audit_verify`, `export_backup`, `import_backup`,
  `REST_SERVICE_TYPE` and `api_base_from_did_document`, plus the three task
  URIs. All are additive.

- **vta**: Contexts/secrets requires KeyExport (VTI-VTA-003) ([#1634](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1634))

`vta/contexts/secrets/1.0` (`get_context_secrets`) released a context DID's
  private keys to any `Application`-role caller in that context. Its only gate
  was the role floor (`require_write`, which also admits `Initiator`) plus the
  context scope. VTI-VTA-003 says an export of derived key material "MUST be
  gated by a capability distinct from the capability to use the key, and MUST
  be audited". The audit was already there; the separate capability was not.
  An `Application` can *use* its context's keys through the signing oracle, and
  under the old gate that also let it *take* them. That is the case the
  requirement exists for: keys that were taken stay with the caller after its
  authority is withdrawn.

Retire marks the face before clearing its bindings, so an interrupted retire leaves a face that cannot be newly worn and a repeat finishes the clearing; the cleared bindings come back in `unbound`. binding/set and local/binding/set refuse a retired face (`profileRetired`), profile/list leaves retired faces out unless `includeRetired`. The storage-thread sweeper (expire_bindings, audited as persona.binding.expire) makes the clear durable and retires a face the expiry left worn nowhere; never one still worn elsewhere, and never deletes. profile/get and profile/delete return `disclosedTo` {partyCount, contextCount}; `pnm persona profile delete` says "deleting does not un-tell them". Local by default: a typed value is carried inline and enters no pool unless the claim says `share: pool`, when a self-asserted pool attribute holding exactly that type and value is referenced, and created only if none exists. Where the face lives follows from its claims — all local makes a context-local face, anything pooled or held a pool face. Everything is validated before anything is written (unresolvedReference, duplicateSlot, labelWithoutPersona), and a later failure removes the attributes the compose created. promote — named entries of a context-local face become pool attributes and the face moves into the pool with its id, name, order, slots and wearers unchanged. One-way. The pool face is written and the bindings moved before the local face is removed, so an interrupted promote leaves the local face worn and a retry finishes it, reusing what it made. versionConflict and entryOutOfRange refuse a stale or out-of-range read. Both holder-only (Reach::Holder), classified Keyed for retry, Mutating for the MCP guard. `pnm persona profile compose` and `pnm persona attribute promote`. All three took a token from `SessionStore::ensure_authenticated`, whose audience is not a parameter: it is always the session's bound *VTA* DID, and the DIDComm authenticate envelope it builds is encrypted to that DID's key-agreement key. A VTC holds only its own keys, cannot open the envelope, and refuses the login. `cnm vetting` then also built its `VtcClient` with the VTA's DID as the community's DID. main connected to the VTA first, so without `--url` the requests went to the VTA's REST URL too. They now authenticate the way `cnm did-log install` does ([#1632](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1632)): `VtcClient::connect(base, vtc_did, client_did, key)` with the profile's DID and key, and the VTC's DID as the audience. They are exempt from `requires_auth`, so no VTA connection is made first. Where the VTC's DID comes from: `--vtc-did` (env `CNM_VTC_DID`), else a new optional `vtc_did` on the community profile, set with `cnm community set-vtc `. The DID is never read from the server (for example the VTC's `/health`): it is the audience the sign-in is signed for, and a server allowed to name it could name another community's DID and relay the signed document there. Discovery runs from DID to URL, as it does for a VTA: `--url` if given, otherwise the `VTCRest` service in the DID's document, matched on `type` and checked by the same endpoint guard as a VTA's advertised REST URL. The root cause is a generic "token for this base URL" helper sitting on a session bound to one audience. `cnm`'s `auth::ensure_authenticated` wrapper is removed, so nothing in `cnm` can reach the VTC through the VTA session again, and `SessionStore::ensure_authenticated` now documents that it authenticates to the session's VTA only. Nothing else in the workspace used `SessionStore` against a VTC. When the VTC refuses the sign-in, `cnm` prints the fix with the DID filled in: `vtc --config acl add --did --role admin --label cnm`, or Access control, Add entry in the console. A VTC answers every authentication failure the same way (VTI-SES-007), so the message names the usual cause rather than claiming it. Routing these through a live VTC exposed two more faults on the same paths, fixed here: - `cnm backup export` saved the `{ envelope }` response (the export shape since #1059) instead of the envelope, so the file printed `(none)` for its source DID and could not be imported. `VtcClient::export_backup` returns the envelope, and accepts a pre-#1059 bare one. - `cnm audit verify` read the signed-checkpoint result from the top level, but #1110 moved it under `ext["org.openvtc"]`. Every report therefore looked like it had no checkpoint result, and a truncated log that the community key contradicts passed as long as its hash chain did. It reads both places now, and fails on any checkpoint status it does not know rather than passing it. vtc-client gains `audit_verify`, `export_backup`, `import_backup`, `REST_SERVICE_TYPE` and `api_base_from_did_document`, plus the three task URIs. All are additive. - **vta**: Contexts/secrets requires KeyExport (VTI-VTA-003) ([#1634](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1634)) `vta/contexts/secrets/1.0` (`get_context_secrets`) released a context DID's private keys to any `Application`-role caller in that context. Its only gate was the role floor (`require_write`, which also admits `Initiator`) plus the context scope. VTI-VTA-003 says an export of derived key material "MUST be gated by a capability distinct from the capability to use the key, and MUST be audited". The audit was already there; the separate capability was not. An `Application` can *use* its context's keys through the signing oracle, and under the old gate that also let it *take* them. That is the case the requirement exists for: keys that were taken stay with the caller after its authority is withdrawn.

A community whose DID is `did:webvh::` serves its own did.jsonl, but the VTA holds the keys that extend it and cannot reach the community's copy, and the VTC keeps no VTA credential after setup. The VTC now answers `did-management/did/register/0.1` — the task a DID owner sends a DID host, where a second register with a longer log is an update — for its own DID at the root slot `.well-known`, over `POST /v1/admin/did/register` (super-admin). Before serving, it verifies the whole log (every entry's proof under the update keys in force, SCID, hash chain), that it is the community's own DID, and that every served entry survives unchanged as a prefix; then swaps the file atomically, with no restart. So an administrator's authority covers delivery only: a log the key holder did not sign, or one that moves the served log backwards, is refused whoever delivers it. The prefix rule is stricter than `register` alone and carries a consumer-minted code (SPEC §8.5). - `cnm did-log install --file did.jsonl`, fed by `pnm did-mgmt dids get-log`. It authenticates to the community directly, with the community's DID as the audience (`VtcClient::connect`), not through the profile's VTA session, whose audience is the VTA's DID — a VTC refuses that. All three took a token from `SessionStore::ensure_authenticated`, whose audience is not a parameter: it is always the session's bound *VTA* DID, and the DIDComm authenticate envelope it builds is encrypted to that DID's key-agreement key. A VTC holds only its own keys, cannot open the envelope, and refuses the login. `cnm vetting` then also built its `VtcClient` with the VTA's DID as the community's DID. main connected to the VTA first, so without `--url` the requests went to the VTA's REST URL too. title: fix(vtc-client)!: upload_policy sends the canonical policy/upsert body; add member_credentials
body:
Both fixes touch `vtc-client/src/lib.rs`, so they are in one PR.

## B. `upload_policy` sent a body the VTC refuses

**Root cause.** `VtcClient::upload_policy` posted `{purpose, regoSource}` to `POST /v1/policies`. The route's `UploadBody` (`vtc-service/src/routes/policies/admin.rs`) is `deny_unknown_fields` and binds `policy/upsert/0.2`. That body requires `{name, module}` and reads the purpose from `ext["org.openvtc.purpose"]`. Every upload was refused before it reached the handler, so the method had never worked against a live VTC. The admin console (`policies-api.ts`) already sent the canonical shape. Only the Rust client was wrong.

**Fix.**
- The client builds the generated `trust_tasks_rs::specs::policy::upsert::v0_2::Payload` (re-exported as `vtc_client::policy_upsert`). It sends `name` = purpose (as the console does), `module` = the Rego source, and `ext["org.openvtc.purpose"]` = purpose (`vtc_client::POLICY_PURPOSE_EXT_KEY`).
- A payload the schema refuses (such as an empty module) is the new `VtcError::InvalidPayload`, and nothing is sent.
- The method's signature is unchanged.

**Server-side, one line.** The generated payload always serialises `enabled` (schema `default: true`), and `UploadBody::unsupported` refused `enabled` whatever its value. So a client built on the canonical type could never be accepted. The VTC now refuses only `enabled: false`, which asks for something it cannot do. `true` asks for nothing. The existing `enabled: false` refusal test still passes. This does not touch the error-code census or the handler error mapping.

## C. No client method for `vtc/members/credentials/0.1`

**Fix.** `VtcClient::member_credentials(did)` calls `GET /v1/members/{did}/credentials` with the `Trust-Task` header, taken from the generated `Payload::TYPE_URI`. It returns the generated `members::credentials::v0_1::Response` (re-exported as `vtc_client::members_credentials`).

The client had no typed errors before this: every failure was `VtcError::Http`. So this PR adds:
- `VtcError::NotFound { code, message }`, produced only for a 404 whose JSON `code` is one of the task's **declared** `ERROR_CODES` (`vtc/members/credentials:notFound`).
- A 404 without a declared code stays `Http`. A VTC that predates the route also answers 404, and that does not mean the member is absent.

## Breaking (`!`)

`VtcError` was exhaustive. It gains `NotFound` and `InvalidPayload`, and it is now `#[non_exhaustive]` so that later typed errors are not breaking changes. All in-workspace matches (`cnm-cli`) already have wildcard arms.

## Tests

- `vtc-service/tests/vtc_client_live.rs`, against `MockVtc::start_with(TestVtc)`:
  - `upload_policy_is_accepted_and_activates`: the upload returns `created: true` with the purpose under `ext`, and the returned id activates.
  - `member_credentials_round_trips_and_types_not_found`: a seeded member's membership credential round-trips into the generated `Response`, and an unknown DID is `VtcError::NotFound` with the declared code.
- `vtc-service/tests/policy_canonical.rs`: `upsert_accepts_enabled_true_the_schema_default`.
- `vtc-client` unit tests: the serialised upload body has the canonical shape; an empty module is refused before sending; only a 404 with a declared code is typed (a bare 404, an undeclared code and a 403 each stay `Http`).

Verification:
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --no-fail-fast` (with the admin-UI build): all green except `openapi_snapshot` on the first run. A doc comment I had changed on `UploadBody` flowed into the OpenAPI document. I moved it to a plain comment, and `openapi_snapshot` and `policy_canonical` then passed on a rerun.
- These runs were on the parent of #1639. #1639 bumps trust-tasks-rs 0.21.14 → 0.21.15, whose `policy/upsert` and `vtc/members/credentials` modules are byte-identical. This PR's files are untouched since then.

title: fix(vta): device bindings list effective capabilities, partitioned by the published enum
body:
## Root cause

`vta-service/src/operations/device.rs::split_capabilities` built a device binding's capability list from the entry's **stored** list whenever it was non-empty, and fell back to the role's derived set only when it was empty.

The stored list does not say what an entry holds. Since #1279 (and #1619's `KeyExport`) it is a narrowing of the role plus any additive grant by name, and `vti_common::acl::effective_capabilities` resolves it. Every gate uses that function. The listing did not, so:

- an entry whose stored list is only an additive grant (`[PersonaHolder]`) holds its **whole role** plus holder authority, but was listed as holding holder authority alone. Every role-derived capability was missing.
- a stored name the role does not carry was listed as held, although no gate honours it.

The same function also decides the `capabilities` / `ext` split, and it had a second, related fault. It split against a hand-kept `PUBLISHED_CAPABILITIES` list of eight names. The published `device/_shared` `Capability` enum (trust-tasks-rs 0.21.14) has since registered `signTrustTask`, `credentialWrite`, `memoryRead`, `memoryWrite`, `roomPresent` and `roomOpen`. All six were reported under `ext.org.openvtc.capabilities`, and a `device/list` `capabilityFilter` naming any of them could never match, because the filter only checks the published half.

## Fix

- `split_capabilities` now lists `effective_capabilities(&entry.role, &entry.capabilities)`.
- The hand-kept list is replaced by `is_published_capability`, which asks the generated `device/list` `Capability` type whether it can read the name. The split now follows the specification through a trust-tasks-rs bump. Capabilities the specification has not registered (`keyExport`, `personaHolder`) stay under `ext`.

**Wire effect:** on `device/list` and `device/register` responses, the six capabilities above move from `ext.org.openvtc.capabilities` to `capabilities`, where the specification puts them.

## Tests

`operations::device` unit tests:
- `an_additive_grant_alone_does_not_hide_the_role`: an Application entry holding only `[PersonaHolder]` lists its role's capabilities, with `personaHolder` under `ext`.
- `a_narrowing_is_bounded_by_the_role`: an Application entry storing `[VaultRead, KeyMint]` lists only `vault-read`.
- `capabilities_the_specification_registers_are_published`: the six registered capabilities are in `capabilities`, and only `keyExport` is under `ext`.
- `local_capabilities_are_split_out_not_dropped`: now tests `keyExport`, since `sign-trust-task` has been published.

Verification:
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: 4757 passed, 0 failed


## For consumers of `device/list` / `device/register`

- **`capabilities` reports the effective set.** It is what `effective_capabilities(role, stored)` returns, the same set every gate checks, not the entry's stored list. A caller reading it before this change saw only the stored list (e.g. `[personaHolder]` alone for a holder grant) and got fewer capabilities than the entry actually holds.
- **`capabilityFilter` matches that same effective, published set.** Before, a filter naming any of the six capabilities listed below never matched; now it does.
- **Six capabilities move from `ext["org.openvtc"].capabilities` to `capabilities`,** because the published `device/_shared` enum now includes them: `signTrustTask`, `credentialWrite`, `memoryRead`, `memoryWrite`, `roomPresent`, `roomOpen`. A client that read any of them from `ext` must read `capabilities` instead. `keyExport` and `personaHolder` stay in `ext`.
- **Known consumers checked:** pnm-browser-plugin sends `capabilityFilter` on `device/list` and never reads device capabilities from `ext`, so it is unaffected. Its `org.openvtc.capabilities` handling is on ACL entries, not devices.

title: feat(pnm): name the console's accounts from the VTA
body:
The mediator console identifies accounts by the mediator's account id, `sha256(did)` in lowercase hex. affinidi/affinidi-tdk-rs#867 (released as `affinidi-messaging-mediator-admin` 0.1.3 and `-tui` 0.1.2) added an address book that shows a nickname in place of a hash. This PR has pnm fill that book from the VTA, so the accounts you already know show up by name.

## What pnm names
Sources go from least to most specific, and a later one overrides an earlier one for the same DID:
1. **ACL entries:** everyone with access to this VTA, by their `label`, or by role when there's no label.
2. **Hosted webvh DIDs** (`list_dids_webvh`), as `context · mnemonic`.
3. **This session's context DIDs:** the same list the DID picker uses, by context name. When a context holds several DIDs, each name also gets the end of its DID.
4. **The VTA itself** (`VTA`) and **this pnm session's `did:key`** (`pnm session`).

- **Not saved:** these names are supplied with `AddressBook::know`, so the VTA stays their source.
- **Your names win:** names you add in the console with `n` are saved to the shared address book (`~/.config/mediator-console/address-book.json`, the same file the standalone `mediator-console` uses), and take precedence.
- **Never fatal:** a source this session may not read (listing ACLs needs an admin) is skipped. Naming must never stop the console opening.

## Also
- **Bracketed paste**, so a DID pasted into the naming form arrives in one piece.
- **One identity listing:** `choose` now takes the identity list, so the list is fetched once for both the picker and the names.
- **README:** a short section on names.
- **Cargo.lock:** `affinidi-messaging-mediator-admin` 0.1.1 → 0.1.3 and `-tui` 0.1.0 → 0.1.2. No manifest or version fields are changed.

## Tests
- **New unit test:** identity choices are named by context, told apart when a context holds several DIDs, and the session is named `pnm session`.
- **Existing picker tests:** unchanged and passing.
- `cargo clippy -p pnm-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check` are clean.

title: feat!: add taskDigestMultibase, so a VWC binds to the witness/session it cites
body:
Adds `taskDigestMultibase`. The only VWC-issuing flow the specifications define requires it, and this crate had no way to produce it.

**Specification dependency:** trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec#56 defines the member in DTG Core Credentials. It is approved but not merged. This PR can merge once #56 is accepted.

## What the specifications require

- **`witness/session/submit/0.1`** (dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf), Conformance item 1: the VWC in the witness's response MUST carry two members. `taskContext` MUST equal the `id` of the `witness/session` document that opened *this* session. `taskDigestMultibase` MUST be that document's *task digest*. The same spec says the member's schema "belongs to DTG Core Credentials". `witness/session/0.1`'s `outcomeEvidence` declares the binding at `/payload/vwc/taskContext` and `/payload/vwc/taskDigestMultibase`. Both are top-level members of the VWC.
- **Trust Tasks §4.9.3** (Binding a Citation to the Document It Names) defines the digest as `multibase(multihash(H(JCS(document ∖ proof))))`:
  - only the **top-level** `proof` is removed; a `proof` inside `payload` is content and stays;
  - `H` is any multihash algorithm, with SHA-256 RECOMMENDED;
  - the encoding is any `DigestMultibase` form (`z` or `u`);
  - a verifier compares **decoded multihash bytes**;
  - a verifier treats an unimplemented algorithm as *unverified*, with no fallback to comparing `id`s.
- **dtgwg-cred-spec#56** makes it a top-level property: "REQUIRED wherever `taskContext` is REQUIRED, OPTIONAL otherwise". It adds the property as the sixth member under §Digest Encoding, so an issuer emits sha2-256 and base58btc. That is a valid narrowing of §4.9.3, and it makes the task digest exactly `digest_multibase_json` computed over a Trust Task document.

## API

| | |
|---|---|
| `DTGCommon::task_digest_multibase` + accessors | A modelled member, so a non-string value is refused at parse time. A VWC without it still deserializes. |
| `task_digest_multibase_json(&doc)` | The task digest. It has its own name because Trust Tasks also defines a *step digest* that includes the `proof`, and the two must not stand in for each other. VTI #1630 fixed exactly that confusion. |
| `DTGCredential::new_vwc_for_session(issuer, subject, from, until, &session, digest, ctx) -> Result` | Reads `taskContext` and `taskDigestMultibase` from the session document, so the pair cannot disagree. The edge digest is REQUIRED. Refuses anything except the opening `witness/session` (`NotAWitnessSession`): a `submit` document, a `#response`, or a document whose `threadId` is not its own `id`, which `witness/session` Conformance item 1 requires. |
| `with_task_citation` / `set_task_citation` | Sets both members from one document, on any credential type (for example a `vetting/session` statement). |
| `cites_task(&doc) -> Result<bool>` | Checks the `id` and recomputes the digest, comparing decoded bytes. A credential with no `taskDigestMultibase` returns `Ok(false)`, never an `id`-only match. An unimplemented algorithm is an error. |
| `new_vwc` | Deprecated, because it cannot set the digest. |

### Why this breaks the API

`DTGCommon` is not `#[non_exhaustive]`. Its fields are public, and every constructor builds it with `..Default::default()`. Adding a field therefore breaks exhaustive struct literals only, which is the same break 0.3.0 made for `credentialStatus`. I chose that over the fully additive alternative, which would keep the member in `DTGCommon::extra`, for two reasons:

- The specification makes the member REQUIRED on every VWC, beside `taskContext`, which is already a modelled field.
- `extra` is documented as holding members this library does *not* model, and it would accept a non-string value without complaint.

Marking `DTGCommon` `#[non_exhaustive]` now would be worse: it forbids `..Default::default()` outside the crate. `new_vwc` keeps its signature and is deprecated rather than given a new required parameter, following the pattern 0.10.0 used for `new_member_vmc` → `_for`.

The wire is unchanged for a credential that lacks the member. An older release carries the member through a round trip in `extra`, so this release has no upgrade-ordering constraint. I have not bumped the version. The CHANGELOG entry is under `[Unreleased]`, and `#[deprecated(since = "0.11.0")]` assumes the next release is 0.11.0.

## Tests (`tests/task_citation.rs`, 22)

- **Vector from a second implementation.** `vetting/session/0.1` prints a session document and the `taskDigestMultibase` of it (`zQmWAWEtpUqE3xd3LUpZ8GryGrZMCqH1A5D7bZcayvEfJTK`). `task_digest_multibase_json` reproduces it. The four steps are also recomputed by hand. The Vetting Statement printed there parses, and `cites_task` accepts it against that session.
- **Proof handling.** The digest ignores a top-level `proof` (signed, unsigned and re-signed copies give one value) and keeps a `proof` nested in `payload`.
- **Round trip.** A session VWC serializes with `taskDigestMultibase` at the top level. It parses back into the modelled field (not `extra`), still cites its session, and `digest_multibase()` agrees with the digest of the wire form.
- **Decoded-bytes comparison.**
  - A base64url (`u…`) spelling of the same multihash is accepted.
  - A sha2-512 multihash returns `UnsupportedDigestAlgorithm`, not `false`.
  - A counterfeit that reuses the session `id` with different content is refused.
  - A VWC with no digest cites nothing.
- **Constructor refusals.** The `submit` document, the `#response`, a mismatched or missing `threadId`, a missing `id`, and an inverted validity window.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all --check`: pass
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`: pass. Also passes with `--no-default-features`.
- `cargo test --all-features`: 186 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo test --no-default-features`: 170 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo doc --no-deps --all-features`: no warnings

## Not addressed here

- **The VWC's type on cred-spec `main`.** It is no longer `WitnessCredential`. The spec now expresses it as a `StatementCredential` under the `dtg:witnessed` predicate profile (dtgwg-cred-spec#45). This crate, `new_vwc_for_session` included, still builds the WD02 `WitnessCredential` shape. That migration is separate work. `taskDigestMultibase` is a top-level member either way, so this change carries over.
- **`vwcDigestMultibase`.** In `witness/session/submit#response` it is taken over the credential **including** its `proof`, unlike every digest this crate computes. `digest_multibase` is the wrong function for it.

Refs OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1068.

title: Witness credentials are reasoned about but never built or verified
body:
## Summary

The ceremony engine treats `WitnessCredential` as a policy fact — with
trusted-issuer, validity and holder-binding predicates — but no VWC is ever
constructed or verified anywhere in the stack. `DTGCredential::new_vwc` and
`digest_multibase` are never called.

## Detail

`WitnessCredential` occurs in `ceremony/verify.rs`, `ceremony/facts.rs`,
`ceremony/evaluate.rs`, `routes/ceremonies.rs` and `policy/default.rs` — in
every case as a `credential_type` string in a fact the policy reasons over, not
as a credential the code builds or checks.

The exacting part is therefore entirely untested here. Per DTG Credentials the
VWC's `credentialSubject.digest` MUST be:

- the SHA-256 hash of the witnessed VRC,
- canonicalised with JCS (RFC 8785),
- encoded as a Multibase-encoded Multihash,
- `sha2-256` (header `0x12`, length `0x20`), base58btc (`z` prefix).

And Security Considerations 4 requires a verifier relying on that binding to
have the referenced VRC in hand, recompute the hash, and compare **decoded
digest bytes rather than encoded strings**.

`dtg-credentials` implements all of this correctly (`DTGCredential::digest`,
`digest_multibase`), including the recent multibase change. Nothing calls it.

## Why it matters

A ceremony can currently reach a decision on the *assertion* that a witness
credential was present, without any code path that could have established it
was valid or that it witnessed the edge in question. Security Considerations 4
is explicit that without recomputing the digest against the referenced VRC, a
VWC "should not be treated as evidence of which edge was witnessed".

## Suggested fix

1. Build VWCs through `new_vwc` on whatever path is meant to issue them.
2. On receipt, recompute the digest against the referenced VRC and compare
   decoded bytes.
3. `taskContext` is REQUIRED on the VWC specifically — see #1065, which is a
   prerequisite rather than a parallel task.

Conformance audit finding **F8**.

title: feat(persona)!: derived provenance, and endorsements as inventory
body:
Implements trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#582 (design note
docs/05-design-notes/persona-context-first.md §5.7).

Provenance::Derived { source, derived_at }: a value taken from a source
the holder connected or supplied — a code-hosting profile, an uploaded
CV — that nobody signed. Previewed as `derived` at the whole rung, never
as attested, and it correlates as a typed value does, since there is no
issuer signature to link. `source` is the kind of source, never a handle
or URL, because provenance reaches the verifier.

Attribute.endorsements: vault ids of credentials in which a third party
endorses the value. Inventory, not evidence — it never touches
provenance and is not disclosed with the value. attribute/put checks
every id against the vault and refuses one it does not hold (a
soft-deleted credential does not count) with `endorsementNotFound`.

title: fix(cnm): vetting, audit and backup authenticate to a VTC with its own DID as audience
body:
`cnm vetting`, `cnm audit verify` and `cnm backup` could not sign in to a
VTC. All three took a token from `SessionStore::ensure_authenticated`, whose
audience is not a parameter: it is always the session's bound *VTA* DID, and
the DIDComm authenticate envelope it builds is encrypted to that DID's
key-agreement key. A VTC holds only its own keys, cannot open the envelope,
and refuses the login. `cnm vetting` then also built its `VtcClient` with the
VTA's DID as the community's DID. main connected to the VTA first, so without
`--url` the requests went to the VTA's REST URL too.

They now authenticate the way `cnm did-log install` does (#1632):
`VtcClient::connect(base, vtc_did, client_did, key)` with the profile's DID
and key, and the VTC's DID as the audience. They are exempt from
`requires_auth`, so no VTA connection is made first.

Where the VTC's DID comes from: `--vtc-did` (env `CNM_VTC_DID`), else a new
optional `vtc_did` on the community profile, set with
`cnm community set-vtc <did>`. The DID is never read from the server (for
example the VTC's `/health`): it is the audience the sign-in is signed for,
and a server allowed to name it could name another community's DID and
relay the signed document there. Discovery runs from DID to URL, as it does
for a VTA: `--url` if given, otherwise the `VTCRest` service in the DID's
document, matched on `type` and checked by the same endpoint guard as a
VTA's advertised REST URL.

The root cause is a generic "token for this base URL" helper sitting on a
session bound to one audience. `cnm`'s `auth::ensure_authenticated` wrapper
is removed, so nothing in `cnm` can reach the VTC through the VTA session
again, and `SessionStore::ensure_authenticated` now documents that it
authenticates to the session's VTA only. Nothing else in the workspace
used `SessionStore` against a VTC.

When the VTC refuses the sign-in, `cnm` prints the fix with the DID filled
in: `vtc --config <config.toml> acl add --did <DID> --role admin --label cnm`,
or Access control, Add entry in the console. A VTC answers every
authentication failure the same way (VTI-SES-007), so the message names the
usual cause rather than claiming it.

Routing these through a live VTC exposed two more faults on the same paths,
fixed here:
- `cnm backup export` saved the `{ envelope }` response (the export shape
  since #1059) instead of the envelope, so the file printed `(none)` for
  its source DID and could not be imported. `VtcClient::export_backup`
  returns the envelope, and accepts a pre-#1059 bare one.
- `cnm audit verify` read the signed-checkpoint result from the top level,
  but #1110 moved it under `ext["org.openvtc"]`. Every report therefore
  looked like it had no checkpoint result, and a truncated log that the
  community key contradicts passed as long as its hash chain did. It reads
  both places now, and fails on any checkpoint status it does not know
  rather than passing it.

vtc-client gains `audit_verify`, `export_backup`, `import_backup`,
`REST_SERVICE_TYPE` and `api_base_from_did_document`, plus the three task
URIs. All are additive.

Tests: `vtc-service/tests/cnm_vtc_admin_live.rs` runs the audit, backup
(export then import preview) and vetting paths against a `MockVtc` over
HTTP. It also checks that a DID with no ACL row is refused in the shape
`cnm` keys its guidance on, and that the old VTA-session login fails where
the VTC-audience login succeeds. `cnm-cli/src/vtc.rs` asserts that the
authenticate document `cnm` sends names the VTC's DID as its `recipient`,
and that the refusal prints the `vtc acl add` command.

Docs: the bootstrap runbook gains the super-admin row `cnm` needs.
community-lifecycle.md and credentials.md listed `cnm join`, `cnm members`,
`cnm policies`, `cnm credentials`, `cnm endorsement-types` and `pnm vtc`
commands that do not exist. They now point at the admin console and REST
routes, and list what `cnm` does provide.


## Verification

- `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --no-fail-fast`: 4748 passed, 0 failed, 50 ignored. The slow `self_hosted_did` 304 test passed after more than 60 s.
- `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --no-fail-fast` (admin UI built): 1779 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean.

## Left open

- The VTC's (and the VTA's) DI-signed `auth/authenticate/0.1` path does not check the document's `recipient`. The DIDComm path is audience-bound by encryption, but the REST path is not, so the server side of the audience binding is missing. Out of scope here.
- `VtcClient::upload_policy` sends `{purpose, regoSource}` to a `deny_unknown_fields` body expecting `{name, module, …}`. Untouched.

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.21.15
body:
### Added

- **persona**: Derived provenance, and endorsements as inventory ([#582](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/582))

Design note (VTI docs/05-design-notes/persona-context-first.md) §5.7.

  Provenance gains `derived` {source, derivedAt}: a value taken from a
  source the holder connected or supplied — a code-hosting profile, an
  uploaded CV — that the holder did not type and no issuer signed. It is
  the holder's claim that the source said so, and a consumer must not
  present it as attested. `source` names the KIND of source (`github`,
  `cvUpload`), never a handle or URL: provenance reaches the verifier, and
  a handle there would disclose an identifier the holder never chose to
  share. For how strongly a disclosed value identifies the holder the
  kinds rank credentialBacked > derived > selfAsserted. The preview's
  provenance enum gains `derived`.

  Attribute gains `endorsements`: vault ids of credentials in which a
  third party endorses the value. Inventory, not evidence — a vouched
  self-assertion is still self-asserted, and folding a vouch into
  provenance would render it as attested. Not disclosed with the value.
  attribute/put takes it and refuses an id the vault does not hold
  (`endorsementNotFound`).

- **spec**: Vtc/invitations/deliver/0.1 — get an invitation to the DID it admits ([#581](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/581))

Keyring VTI-21 and VTI-32. `vtc/invitations/issue` returns the signed
  invitation to the inviter once, and nothing carried it further: an
  invitee was reached only by whatever the inviter improvised, and the
  credential is too large for a QR code.

  This task delivers an issued invitation over the credential-exchange
  family the framework already has. On `message` the community sends a
  `credential-exchange/offer` to the invited DID over a transport it
  advertises (`noRoute` if none); on `offer` it returns the OID4VCI offer
  for the inviter to hand over — small, because it names the credential
  rather than containing it. Either way the invitee redeems with
  `credential-exchange/request`, and the credential is released only for a
  key-binding proof by the invited DID's key, so a photographed QR code
  admits no one else. At most one offer per invitation is live; the
  invitation credential never appears in this task's response.

  Bindings regenerated for Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart.

title: test(vtc): every declared error code must be shown emitted, or baselined (#1600)
body:
The conformance ledgers witness the success path only (#1600). A spec could
declare extended codes, the service could emit none of them, and every gate
stayed green. `withdraw/0.1` shipped that way: its handler answered both
declared codes through the generic `app_error_to_reject` as a bare
`taskFailed`.

Since trust-tasks-rs 0.21.13 (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#575), the
bindings carry each specification's declared `errorCodes`, as `ERROR_CODES`, a
per-task `error_codes` module, and `schema_index::error_codes_for`. The
workspace already requires 0.21.14 (#1635); this derives a census from those
codes.

`vtc-service/src/trust_tasks/error_code_census.rs` takes its scope from the
same bound ∩ published `spec/vtc/*` set as `conformance.rs`, and gets the
declared codes from `error_codes_for`. No code strings are written by hand.
Every declared code must either have a `witness!` row naming the integration
test that asserts the service emits it, or appear in a typed, shrink-only
baseline whose length is asserted. For a witness, the census checks that the
named test exists, asserts on an emitted code (`tt_error_code(` for a Trust
Task error document, `rest_error_code(` for a REST-only route's body) and
names the witness constant, and that the constant's value equals the declared
code. `CONSUMER_MINTED` holds codes the service emits but the spec does not
declare (`submit:requestAlreadyOpen`), and fails once a spec declares one.

Today: 88 declared codes in scope, 10 witnessed, 78 baselined. The census
caught `members/credentials:notFound` from #1631 on its first run against
main: the code was emitted and tested, but spelled as a literal. It is now
read from the generated binding and witnessed.

vta-sdk's `JOIN_REQUEST_*_ERR_*` and `VETTING_*_ERR_*` constants, and
vtc-service's `MEMBER_CREDENTIALS_ERR_NOT_FOUND`, now read the generated
`error_codes::*.code`, so none of them can name an undeclared code. The
exception is the consumer-minted `requestAlreadyOpen`.

Still open under #1600: shrinking the 78-code baseline, the shared
`spec/{acl,audit,auth,config,policy}/*` URIs, and a vta-service equivalent.


Refs #1600. This lands the census; the issue stays open for the 78-code baseline.

## Verification

This was rebased onto main after #1635 moved the workspace to `trust-tasks-rs` 0.21.14, so the PR no longer changes `Cargo.toml` or `Cargo.lock`. Before the rebase, all four CI commands passed: workspace tests 4742 passed / 0 failed, VTC tests 1775 passed / 0 failed, and clippy `-D warnings` and fmt clean. After the rebase fmt passes, and the full set is rerunning. I'll post the results here.

uploaded CV — that the holder did not type and no issuer signed. It is
the holder's claim that the source said so, and a consumer must not
present it as attested. `source` names the KIND of source (`github`,
`cvUpload`), never a handle or URL: provenance reaches the verifier, and
a handle there would disclose an identifier the holder never chose to
share. For how strongly a disclosed value identifies the holder the
kinds rank credentialBacked > derived > selfAsserted. The preview's
provenance enum gains `derived`.

Attribute gains `endorsements`: vault ids of credentials in which a
third party endorses the value. Inventory, not evidence — a vouched
self-assertion is still self-asserted, and folding a vouch into
provenance would render it as attested. Not disclosed with the value.
attribute/put takes it and refuses an id the vault does not hold
(`endorsementNotFound`).

title: feat(persona)!: where a face may be worn, where it is, and what it has done
body:
Implements trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#577 (design note
docs/05-design-notes/persona-context-first.md §5.4, §9.6).

Face reach. A pool face carries `reach` — FaceReach::Anywhere (default)
or Only { context_ids } — an enum rather than a context list, so
unrestricted and nowhere cannot be confused (#746/#769/#770).
binding/set refuses a face outside its reach (`outsideReach`);
profile/put refuses to narrow it past a context the face is worn in
(`boundOutsideReach`, naming them). An omitted reach on profile/put keeps
the face's current one: a client written before reach existed must not
lift a restriction by saving an edit.

persona/profile/usage — where a face is worn now, each binding's
`until`, and the reach beside them.

persona/profile/timeline — one face's history, oldest first: composed,
worn, unworn, expired, disclosed, valueChanged, promoted, retired,
reinstated. A binding taken off left no trace, so each face now has an
append-only event log (`pft:`, agent-scoped, ULID-keyed so recording
never takes the write lock), written after the change it describes and
never failing it; the timeline joins it with the disclosure records. A
face from before the log reports its composition from createdAt. A
promoted face keeps its log; a deleted one loses it. FaceEvent has no
member a value or label could go in, and a test holds that none reaches
the wire.

profile/compose takes `until` (`untilNotFuture`).

`pnm persona profile usage|timeline`, `put --reach-only/--reach-anywhere`,
`compose --until`. Takes trust-tasks-rs 0.21.14.

ComposeRefusal a variant; VtaClient::persona_profile_put takes `reach`;

title: feat(spec): vtc/invitations/deliver/0.1 — get an invitation to the DID it admits
body:
Adds **`vtc/invitations/deliver/0.1`**: a way to get an issued invitation to the DID it admits. This answers Keyring's VTI-21 (no channel delivers an invitation) and VTI-32 (an invitation is too large for a QR code).

## Why a task, and why so small

`vtc/invitations/issue` returns the signed invitation to the inviter **once**. Nothing carried it further, so an invitee was reached only by whatever the inviter improvised. The credential is also too large to fit in a QR code.

This task doesn't define new delivery machinery. It uses the **credential-exchange family the framework already has**:

- **`channel: "message"`:** the community sends a `credential-exchange/offer` to the invited DID, over a transport that DID advertises. If it advertises none, the answer is `noRoute`.
- **`channel: "offer"`:** the community returns the OID4VCI Credential Offer to the inviter, to hand over out of band. It's small enough for a QR code because it *names* the credential rather than containing it.

Either way, the invitee redeems it with `credential-exchange/request` and receives the credential in `credential-exchange/issue`.

## The property that matters

The offer's pre-authorized code redeems **only** for a `credential-exchange/request` whose key-binding proof is made with a key of the invited DID. So:

- a photographed QR code, a misdirected message or a logged offer admits no one else. That's why `exposure.discloses` is `metadata`, while `issue` is `secret`.
- the invitation credential itself never appears in this task's response; it reaches only the invitee.
- at most one offer per invitation is live, because a new delivery replaces the previous one.

## Checks

- `npm run validate` passes for all 472 specs. The validator caught a local `expired` code shadowing the standard §8.3 `expired`, so the spec now uses the bare standard code.
- The Rust, TypeScript, Go and Dart bindings are regenerated, and `check-bindings` shows all four agree, 897 declared error codes included.
- `cargo test --workspace` passes with 923 tests and 0 failed.
- The negative examples run under `--features validate,vtc`: `request_example_1`, `response_example_1` and `rejects_invalid_examples` all pass.
- `npm run build` passes.
- No versions or CHANGELOGs are touched; release-plz owns those.

The implementation in OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure follows once this is released. The VTC already has the OID4VCI offer store and key-binding verification (`credentials::exchange::{make_offer, redeem}`).

title: fix(acl): key-export and persona-holder, and a narrowing that means what it says
body:
Follow-up to VTI #1619, and a re-sync of `acl-capabilities.json`, which had fallen **two** capabilities behind vti-common 0.21.0.

## The snapshot

- **`key-export`** (VTI #1619) is derived by `admin` alone. Exporting a key is gated separately from using it (VTI-VTA-003), so `initiator` keeps `key-mint` and does not get this.
- **`persona-holder`** is *additive*: no role derives it, and the agent grants it only to entries that name it. The sync script now parses `ADDITIVE_CAPABILITIES` into the snapshot. It fails loudly if that list is missing, rather than writing a snapshot that says there are none.

## Fixed: the console disagreed with the agent's rule

The agent (`vti_common::acl::effective_capabilities`) narrows an entry only by its **non-additive** names, then adds the additive ones on top.

The console intersected the role with the *whole* list. So an entry granted only `persona-holder` computed as holding **nothing**, when the agent gives it the full role plus the pool. `checkNarrowing` also refused `persona-holder` because no role includes it. The agent skips that role check for additive names and instead checks the *granter* (super-admin only), which the console can't see.

## Fixed: the access pane's editor could do the opposite of what it said

- **"Narrow" with nothing ticked sent `[]`**, under a warning that the entry "would be able to do none of what the role allows". The agent reads `[]` as *clear the narrowing*, which means the whole role. So the button meant to take everything away actually restored everything. A narrowing to nothing can't be expressed, so the button is now disabled with an explanation, and the way to take a role's authority away is a role change.
- **"Clear narrowing" sent `[]`**, which silently revoked `persona-holder`. It also stayed enabled on an entry whose only stored name was additive, where there was nothing to clear.

Both now go through a new core function, `narrowingToSend(kept, stored, intent)`. It carries additive grants through, and refuses a narrowing to nothing. The pane edits only the role's own capabilities and shows additive grants on their own line.

## Tests

- New tests in `acl.capabilities.mjs`: the additive list matches the snapshot; no role derives an additive capability; `key-export` is admin's alone; effective sets are right with additive grants alone and alongside a narrowing; `narrowingToSend` keeps the grant, clears without revoking it, and refuses a narrowing to nothing (each refusal paired with the acceptance it borders).
- Whole workspace: `npm run build`, `npm run lint` and `npm test` pass (124 + 668 + 750 + 6 + 9 tests, 0 failed).

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.21.13
body:
### Added

- **rs**: Emit each specification's declared error codes ([#575](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/575))

A specification's `errorCodes` front matter (SPEC §7.3 item 9) never reached
  the Rust bindings, so an implementation could only spell a declared extended
  code as a string literal, and nothing checked the literal was a code the
  specification declares — or that the service emitted the codes it declares at
  all. Downstream, that let `vtc/join-requests/withdraw/0.1` ship answering both
  of its declared codes as a bare `taskFailed` with every gate green
  (OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1600).

  `trust-tasks-codegen` now emits, for every generated module:

  - `pub const ERROR_CODES: &[DeclaredErrorCode]` — the declarations in order,
    empty when the specification declares none;
  - `pub mod error_codes` (when it declares any) — one `DeclaredErrorCode`
    constant per code, named for its local part in SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE
    (`vtc/join-requests/withdraw:notFound` -> `error_codes::NOT_FOUND`), with the
    declared `meaning` as its rustdoc;

  and `schema_index::error_codes_for(type_uri)` serves the same slice by bare
  request Type URI, so a consumer can derive a declared-vs-emitted census rather
  than hand-maintain one. `Some(&[])` (declares nothing) and `None` (unknown URI)
  are distinct answers.

  `DeclaredErrorCode` is a new `#[non_exhaustive]` type carrying `code` (the
  fully qualified wire string, usable in a `const`) and `retryable` (as
  declared), with `namespace()`, `local()` and `matches(&TrustTaskCode)`. It
  converts infallibly into `TrustTaskCode`, and into `ErrorPayload` with the
  declared `retryable` rather than the §8.5 default. There is deliberately no
  `PartialEq<DeclaredErrorCode> for TrustTaskCode`: a second `PartialEq` impl
  makes every existing `assert_eq!(code, StandardCode::X.into())` ambiguous.

  The generator refuses a declaration whose code does not parse, whose namespace
  is neither the slug nor a path prefix of it (§8.5 rule 2), or whose local part
  collides with another declaration's constant. `check-bindings` now compares
  every Rust `ERROR_CODES` against the front matter, re-derived independently
  (891 codes across 464 modules). TypeScript, Go and Dart do not emit error codes
  yet; CLAUDE.md records that as the follow-up.

  Additive only: new items, a new type and new `From` impls.
