title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.21.11
body:
### Added

- **persona**: Compose a face where it is asked for, and promote a local value ([#569](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/569))

* feat(persona): compose a face where it is asked for, and promote a local value

  persona/profile/compose/1.0 — a holder composes a face for one context
  at the moment the context asks for one, from values typed there and
  attributes already held, and may wear it in the same act. Local by
  default: a typed value stays in the face and enters no pool unless the
  claim says `share: pool`, in which case the maintainer references a pool
  attribute holding exactly that value, creating one only when none
  exists. Where the face lives follows from its claims — every claim local
  makes a context-local face, anything pooled makes a pool face — so there
  is no scope parameter a producer could set wrongly.

  persona/attribute/promote/1.0 — the deliberate widening: named entries
  of a context-local face become pool attributes, and the face moves above
  contexts with its id, order, slots and bindings unchanged. One-way,
  because the pool attribute may by then be presented elsewhere; the step
  order is specified so a failure part-way leaves the local face worn and
  a retry completes it.

  Both holder-authorized and unscoped. Design: VTI
  docs/05-design-notes/persona-context-first.md §2.1, §5.3.



### Specifications

- Generate SPEC.md from the canonical framework specification ([#559](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/559))

SPEC.md was a hand-ported copy of trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-spec,
  and had drifted: it lacked #14's versioning sections (Document Status,
  three-part framework versions, ratification), among others. It is now an
  output.

  - scripts/generate-framework-spec.mjs assembles the canonical Spec-Up-T
    sources (specs.json markdown_paths + term definitions), numbers the
    headings in canonical order, rewrites named anchors to numbered ones,

title: spec: serve and resolve three-part framework versions
body:
Aligns the registry with the framework's three-part versioning (SPEC §5.1.1, now on the site since #559). This is the follow-up noted on #559.

## Why: a live breakage

Since framework **0.4.0**, which adopted the rule, the framework's Type URI has been `https://trusttasks.org/spec/trust-task/<MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH>`. 61 specs already declare `targetFrameworkVersion: "0.5.0"`. But the CloudFront function only accepts `M.N`, so the URI those specs name fails today:

```
/spec/trust-task/0.5    Accept: application/schema+json -> 200 application/json
/spec/trust-task/0.5.0  Accept: application/schema+json -> 200 text/html   <- the SPA shell
```

A consumer following §7.2 item 1 for any of those 61 specs gets HTML under a 200.

The build had the matching bug in reverse: `frameworkMinor` truncated any `M.N.P` to `M.N`. That validates a future `0.6.1` target against `0.6.0`, which is exactly the PATCH substitution §5.1.1 forbids.

## What changes

**CloudFront (`infra/cloudfront/type-uri-negotiation.js`):**

| Request (`Accept: application/schema+json`) | Served from |
|---|---|
| `/spec/trust-task/M.N.0` | `_framework/M.N/`, where a `.0` release is stored once |
| `/spec/trust-task/M.N.P` (P > 0) | `_framework/M.N.P/`, never its `.0` |
| `/spec/trust-task/M.N` | unchanged: `_framework/M.N/`, the alias of `.0` |
| three-part version on a task slug | refused (task versions are two-part) |

Covered by new infra tests (24 pass), `verify.sh` checks for `0.5.0` and `0.6.0`, and a README section on updating the published function.

**Build (`scripts/build-registry.mjs`):**
- `frameworkEnvelopeKey` resolves the exact release with the same mapping as CloudFront.
- A spec or binding whose target names no published release now **fails**. Before, it warned and left its examples unvalidated.
- A **two-part target naming 0.5 or later fails**, with "declare `0.5.0`". 0.4.0 adopted the rule, and specs "published or re-issued from this version onward" must declare three-part. So a two-part `0.5`+ can't be a pre-rule declaration. Two-part `0.1`–`0.4` remain valid (they resolve as `M.N.0`). Retired specs are frozen (§5.3) and exempt.
- Each envelope's `$id` is checked against its directory: three-part from 0.4 on (the release that adopted the rule), two-part for 0.1–0.3.
- Binding prose claims ("Targets **framework `…`**") may be three-part.

**Envelope `$id`s:** `_framework/0.4`, `0.5` and `0.6` now carry their three-part Type URIs (`…/0.4.0`, `…/0.5.0`, `…/0.6.0`). 0.4.0's own changelog says "this document's Type URI becomes `…/0.4.0`". Nothing references the old `$id`s, and the two-part URIs are still served as aliases.

**Normalisation (most of the file count):** the **351 draft specs, 5 bindings and 1 ceremony** that declared `"0.5"` now declare `"0.5.0"`. The bindings' "Targets **framework `…`**" prose line changes with them. This is editorial, with no wire effect: both values select the same envelope, and CONTRIBUTING-SPECS allows re-pinning a framework in place on a draft. `rooms/keys/present/0.1` is retired and left as is. Generated bindings don't embed the value; `check-bindings` still agrees.

**Ceremonies:** `ceremony.meta.schema.json` accepts three-part, and `validate-ceremonies` applies the same after-the-rule check. A new fixture case covers it (21/21 rejected).

**Meta-schema:** the `targetFrameworkVersion` description now states the rule.

## Checks
- `npm run build` (strict): passes, and 703 example documents are validated against their envelopes.
- `check-bindings`: all agree; regeneration produced no changes.
- `test:infra`: 24/24.
- `validate-ceremonies` and `--test`: pass.
- Negative tests:
  - target `"0.5"` on a draft fails and asks for `"0.5.0"`;
  - target `"0.6.1"` fails because no such release exists;
  - target `"0.5.0"` passes;
  - an envelope with a two-part `$id` (from 0.4 on) fails.

## ⚠️ After merge: publish the CloudFront function

The website deploy does **not** update the function; it's published by hand (`infra/cloudfront/README.md`, "Update the published function"). Until it is, `/spec/trust-task/0.5.0` keeps returning the shell. Then run `./verify.sh`.

## Not in this PR
- **`trust-task-discovery/0.1`'s `frameworkVersion` is two-part only.** Its published schema pattern is `^M.N$`, so a responder can't advertise a three-part release over the wire. That needs a `trust-task-discovery/0.2` plus library changes. The library defaults are also stale: Rust advertises `"0.2"`, Dart `'0.5'`.

title: vta-service-v0.37.1
body:
### Fixed

- **trust-tasks**: Name an upstream failure as one, not as an internal error ([#1609](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1609))

A `ServiceError` at 502/504 — a DID-hosting server or other peer that did
  not answer or refused — fell into the catch-all arm and went out as an
  opaque `internalError`. An openvtc join that failed because the hosting
  server's replies were refused by its mediator (`e.p.limits.queue.sender`)
  showed the user "internal error: the consumer could not complete this
  task", pointing at their own VTA.

  It now goes out as `taskFailed` with `details.reason` =
  `upstream_unavailable` and fixed text. The cause (peer, URL, its body)
  stays in the operator's log, as the framework requires. The SDK recovers
  the reason as `VtaError::Server { status: 502 }`, the variant REST
  already produces for the same failure.

title: feat(acl)!: `key-export` is its own capability, and minting a DID needs `KeyMint`, not admin
body:
Keyring finding VTI-23: `webvh/dids/create` and `keys/export-secret` both checked
for the admin role, so a least-privilege manager was impossible for the persona
lifecycle — an `initiator` holds `KeyMint` and `Sign` and was refused both.

## Minting a DID: `KeyMint`

Minting a DID mints its keys, which `initiator` is already trusted to do. The
gate in `create_did_webvh` is now `KeyMint`, so a manager on `initiator` can mint
personas. The context check is unchanged and still bounds *where*.

It reads the caller's **entry**, so a narrowing that removes `KeyMint` stops the
next call — the rule every capability gate has followed since #1279. That needs
the ACL keyspace in `CreateDidWebvhDeps`, as `acl_ks: Option<&KeyspaceHandle>`:
`Some` from both live constructors and from provisioning; `None` only for the
offline CLI and first-boot setup, whose claims are synthesized under a DID that is
deliberately in no ACL — so reading the store would find no entry and fall back to
the role anyway. The gate is extracted as `ensure_may_mint` so it can be tested as
the code that runs, rather than by a test that mirrors it.

## Exporting a key: a new `KeyExport` capability

VTI-VTA-003 is normative here:

> Where a VTA supports exporting derived key material, that export MUST be gated
> by a capability distinct from the capability to use the key, and MUST be
> audited.

The admin-role check was not that. It coupled export to being an admin, so export
could neither be granted below admin nor narrowed away from one. `KeyExport` is
now the gate; scope and auditing inside `get_key_secret` are unchanged.

**Only `admin` derives it.** That is deliberate, and it is the answer to the half
of VTI-23 this does not grant. An `initiator` holds `Sign`, which is the signing
oracle — its whole guarantee is that the key never leaves — and VTI-VTA-002 makes
performing the operation the norm and exporting it the exception, because an
exported key stays with whoever holds it after their authority is withdrawn. A
manager that needs to act as a persona signs through the oracle.

`KeyExport` is role-derived, not additive, so naming it on an `initiator` grants
nothing. Making it both admin-derived *and* grantable would need a change to
`effective_capabilities`' invariant (a capability is either derived or additive,
never both), which was considered and not taken.

## One behaviour change to know about

An admin who was **narrowed** under #1279 could export until now, because the
role check ignored narrowing. Their stored set could not name `key-export` — it
did not exist — so after this they cannot. That is the narrowing working as
intended, closing the one power it could not previously restrict. Un-narrowed
admins keep everything.

`KeyExport` is not in the published `device/_shared/0.2` enum, and
`PUBLISHED_CAPABILITIES` lists that enum positively, so it lands in `ext` as an
ecosystem-local capability rather than leaking into a closed schema.

## Follow-up outside this repository

The TS console keeps a hand-maintained copy of the role table
(`acl-capabilities.json`, synced from this repo's `origin/main`). It must be
re-synced after this merges, or it will under-report an admin's authority.

## Tests

- Role table: admin derives `KeyExport`; no other role does; it narrows away
  from an admin; naming it on an initiator grants nothing.
- `keys/export-secret`: an initiator is refused at the gate; an admin passes it;
  a narrowed admin is refused. The last is the one the old role floor would have
  let through — verified by restoring it.
- `ensure_may_mint`: an initiator may mint; a reader may not; a narrowing
  without `KeyMint` stops the next mint — verified to fail when the entry is
  ignored; offline callers fall back to the role.

title: spec: generate SPEC.md from the canonical framework specification
body:
Makes `SPEC.md` a **generated copy** of the canonical framework specification (trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-spec), and has trusttasks.org serve the one generated from canonical `main`.

## Why

`SPEC.md` was ported by hand and had drifted. Comparing the live trusttasks.org copy with canonical `main`: canonical #14 (Document Status semver, three-part framework versions, the ratification rules) never reached it, so the site served none of those sections. The outcome-evidence text was only in sync because it was copied across by hand in #550 and #555.

## How

**`scripts/generate-framework-spec.mjs`** (`npm run generate-framework-spec`):
- **Source:** fetches canonical `main` by default. `--ref <sha>` pins a commit, `--from <dir>` uses a local checkout, and `--check` exits 1 if `SPEC.md` differs.
- **Assembly:** joins the canonical `specs.json` `markdown_paths`, and renders the Spec-Up-T term definitions into Terminology.
- **Numbering and links:** numbers headings in canonical order (appendices become A–C), rewrites canonical named anchors to numbered ones, and renders `[[ref: …]]` in italics.
- **Banner:** a do-not-edit notice naming the canonical commit it was generated from.

**`scripts/framework-spec-legacy-anchors.json`:** every anchor of the old hand-maintained copy, mapped to its canonical section. The generator emits each one as an `<a id>` alias on the right heading, so existing links and external bookmarks keep resolving. It fails if an alias would collide with a different section's anchor.

**Registry build: a new check that every link into `SPEC.md` resolves.** Every `/SPEC.md#…` link in spec and binding prose, including the bindings' absolute GitHub links, must name a section or an alias (1,421 links today). Before this, the build only checked that the file existed. The check found **15 links already broken** against the old copy, and they're fixed here:
- 12 × `#64-error-documents` → §8.1
- 1 × `#101-replay` → §12.1
- 1 × `#410-error-codes` → §4.10
- 2 × `#84-retries-and-idempotency` → §8.4

That's 15 link occurrences across 14 files.

**Deploy (`deploy.yml`):**
- Regenerates `SPEC.md` from canonical `main` **before** the build, so every link is checked against the text that will be served.
- Warns, without failing, if the committed copy is behind.
- Adds a daily schedule plus `workflow_dispatch` and `repository_dispatch` (`framework-spec-updated`), so canonical changes reach the site without waiting for a push here.

**Docs:** `CLAUDE.md`, `CONTRIBUTING-SPECS.md`, `README.md` and the website's framework page now point framework changes at the canonical repository.

## Renumbering

Numbers now follow canonical order. §4–§9 are unchanged. What moves:

| Old | New |
|---|---|
| §2 Terminology | §3 |
| §3 Conformance | §17 |
| §10 Security & Privacy (§10.1–§10.4) | §12 Security (§12.1–§12.4) |
| §10.5 Identifier correlation | §13.1 (Privacy) |
| §11 Discovery | §10 (subsections follow canonical order) |
| §12 Task control | §11 |
| §13 References | §18 |

165 qualified references (`SPEC §N`, `SPEC.md §N`, and the `§` form inside schema JSON) and 35 link fragments are rewritten across specs, bindings, docs, scripts and library doc comments. Unqualified `§N` is left alone, because in this repository it refers to a binding's own sections or to another document (e.g. "binding §2", "RFC 9110 §15"). Bindings are regenerated.

## Checks
- `npm run build` (strict Security & Privacy): passes; 1,421 framework links resolve.
- `npm run check-bindings`: all four languages agree.
- `npm run test:infra`: passes.
- `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs -p trust-tasks-https`: passes.
- `trust-tasks-ts`: 79/79.
- `node scripts/generate-framework-spec.mjs --check` against live canonical `main` (f2a4b67): matches.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)
Canonical #14 makes the framework's Type URI and every target framework version **three-part** (`0.6.0`). The registry still uses two-part values (`_framework/0.6`, `$id …/trust-task/0.6`, `targetFrameworkVersion: "0.5"`). This PR makes that rule visible on the site. Aligning the registry with it is a separate change.

title: cnm-cli-v0.17.0
body:
### Added

- **vtc**: A community can ask an applicant to tell it about themselves ([#1614](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1614))

Implements trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#543 (trust-tasks-rs 0.21.9),
  design note docs/05-design-notes/persona-context-first.md §5.2. A join
  manifest could ask only for credentials, so a community wanting a
  display name had nothing to put on the "what's required" screen, and
  nothing connected the join ceremony to an applicant's persona.

  - Requested attributes are one community-level row beside the branding
    (`community/requested-attributes`, backed up with it), managed with
    admin GET/PUT /v1/community/requested-attributes (audited:
    CommunityRequestedAttributesUpdated, types added/removed only), and
    published as `requestedAttributes` on join-requests/manifest/0.2.
  - join-requests/submit/0.2 accepts `attributes`. Before anything is
    stored -- before the open-request dedup -- the answers are checked:
    a required type unanswered is attributesMissing, a type the manifest
    does not request is attributesUnrequested (refused, not trimmed), both
    with details.types. Accepted answers are stored on the request and
    returned by show/list as `attributes`. They are self-asserted and are
    never fed to the join policy.
  - Only the Trust Task form carries them: the legacy REST submit's holder
    signature covers a fixed member set that does not include them, so an
    answer there would be unsigned. A community that requires one refuses
    that route with attributesMissing.
  - VtcClient::requested_attributes / set_requested_attributes, and
    `cnm vetting ask show|set --require/--optional/--purpose/--nothing`.
  - vta_sdk::openapi gains JoinManifest02RequestedAttribute, rendered from
    the specification's own schema by JSON pointer (`Name@<pointer>`),
    because the spec declares the item inline; admin-ui openapi.json and
    wire.ts regenerated.

title: vta-cli-common-v0.20.1
body:
### Fixed

- **cli**: A serverless mint says the operator must host it, and a hosted one says nothing ([#1616](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1616))

Keyring finding VTI-20. `pnm did-mgmt dids create` returns the new DID's log
  entry for **both** kinds of mint, and printed the same advice for both:

      To self-host this DID, place the log entry in a file named `did.jsonl`
      at the URL path corresponding to your DID URL.

  That was wrong in each direction:

  - **Serverless**, it read as one option among several, when it is the only way
    the DID will ever resolve. The VTA that minted it does not serve it; its URL
    answers 404 until someone publishes the file by hand.
  - **Server-managed**, it told the operator to do something the hosting server
    had already done.

  The advice now branches on `server_id`. A serverless mint says plainly that the
  DID will not resolve until the operator publishes it, and where it goes — the
  `--did-url` path, or `/.well-known/did.jsonl` for a bare domain, which is the
  `didwebvh-rs` mapping. A server-managed mint names the server and says no action
  is needed.

  The exact URL is described rather than computed. Computing it would mean adding
  `didwebvh-rs` as a real dependency of `vta-cli-common` (it is only a
  dev-dependency of `vta-sdk`), or a new member on a published wire type — both
  out of proportion to one line of output, and the finding asked only that the
  output say serverless means *you* host it.

  Two similar messages in `vta-service` (the offline `vta did-webvh` path and the
  setup wizard) are left as they are: different surfaces, the first already names
  the exact URL, and neither is what was reported.

title: fix(onboard): store an added agent when it connects; update dependencies
body:
Adding a second trust agent looked like it worked, but the agent never showed up in the popup's list of VTAs. It happened twice in a row.

### Cause
From the setup page's **+ Connect another trust agent**, a successful connect put the connection in component state and saved it only when the operator clicked **Encrypt** or **Skip** on the "Wallet onboarded ✓" screen. That screen reads as the end, so people closed the tab there. By then:
- the agent had already written the ACL entry;
- the offscreen document had already stored the holder key;
- the wallet had not recorded the agent.

### Fix
- **Store on connect.** `OnboardView` saves the connection as soon as connect succeeds. The encrypt prompt is now an optional step that only re-wraps the key; leaving it closes the add-another panel. The key can still be encrypted later from the plaintext banner.
- **Reload the store when another page writes it.** Each extension page loaded the persisted `pnm-connection/v3` map once, and every write replaced the whole blob. A page loaded before another page added an agent would write its old map back over it. The store now reloads when `storage.onChanged` reports a write from another page. Its own writes are recognised and skipped, and `hydrate` doesn't persist, so this can't loop.
- **Keep `homeContext` / `agentScope` through a transport refresh.** The popup rebuilt the connection from a hand-picked list that left both out, so any transport change erased them and the setup page then said "not recorded". `withRefreshedTransports` (`store.ts`) replaces only the three transport members.

### Dependencies
- `@openvtc/trust-tasks` ^0.19.14 → ^0.19.17, at the root and in core.
- `@types/chrome` ^0.2.2 → ^0.3.0 (extension). No code changes were needed.
- In the pwa: `@tanstack/react-query` ^5.103.2, `lucide-react` ^1.47.0, `react-router-dom` ^7.18.4.
- The lockfile is refreshed within existing ranges (rolldown, rollup, `@types/node`, among others).
- The `@swc` override stays at `~1.15.47`; the plugin break it guards against is still unfixed.

### Checks
- Cold `npm run clean` → `npm run lint` → `npm run build` → `npm test`: 1550 passed, 0 failed.
- Every CI assertion on `dist/` passes locally: the single-bundle worker and console, the admin, seeds and persona guards, the Web Store zip, and pinned commits.
- New tests: `connection-store-sync.test.mts` (2 tests), plus one rendered test in `onboard-scope.render.test.mts`. All 3 fail on main and pass here.

### Pre-merge checklist (vti-stack-development-guide §9)
- [x] No new bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2): no network code touched
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3): n/a
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect (R2.1): the connection is now saved *after* the agent and offscreen report success, which is the point of the fix
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off (R1.4): n/a
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5): n/a
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6): inbound path not touched
- [x] New/changed wire types (R3.*): none
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive (R5.*): n/a
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified (R6.*): "Wallet onboarded ✓" is now true when it is shown
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1): closing the page at any point after connect leaves a stored, working (unencrypted) connection
- [x] No deviations from the guide

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

A join manifest could ask only for credentials, so a community wanting a display name had nothing to put on the "what's required" screen, and nothing connected the join ceremony to an applicant's persona. - Requested attributes are one community-level row beside the branding (`community/requested-attributes`, backed up with it), managed with admin GET/PUT /v1/community/requested-attributes (audited: CommunityRequestedAttributesUpdated, types added/removed only), and published as `requestedAttributes` on join-requests/manifest/0.2. - join-requests/submit/0.2 accepts `attributes`. Before anything is stored -- before the open-request dedup -- the answers are checked: a required type unanswered is attributesMissing, a type the manifest does not request is attributesUnrequested (refused, not trimmed), both with details.types. Accepted answers are stored on the request and returned by show/list as `attributes`. They are self-asserted and are never fed to the join policy. - Only the Trust Task form carries them: the legacy REST submit's holder signature covers a fixed member set that does not include them, so an answer there would be unsigned. A community that requires one refuses that route with attributesMissing. - VtcClient::requested_attributes / set_requested_attributes, and `cnm vetting ask show|set --require/--optional/--purpose/--nothing`. - vta_sdk::openapi gains JoinManifest02RequestedAttribute, rendered from the specification's own schema by JSON pointer (`Name@`), because the spec declares the item inline; admin-ui openapi.json and wire.ts regenerated.
## `vta-cli-common`
## [0.20.1](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vta-cli-common-v0.20.0...vta-cli-common-v0.20.1) — 2026-09-21 ### Fixed - **cli**: A serverless mint says the operator must host it, and a hosted one says nothing ([#1616](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1616)) Keyring finding VTI-20. `pnm did-mgmt dids create` returns the new DID's log entry for **both** kinds of mint, and printed the same advice for both: To self-host this DID, place the log entry in a file named `did.jsonl` at the URL path corresponding to your DID URL. That was wrong in each direction: - **Serverless**, it read as one option among several, when it is the only way the DID will ever resolve. The VTA that minted it does not serve it; its URL answers 404 until someone publishes the file by hand. - **Server-managed**, it told the operator to do something the hosting server had already done. The advice now branches on `server_id`. A serverless mint says plainly that the DID will not resolve until the operator publishes it, and where it goes — the `--did-url` path, or `/.well-known/did.jsonl` for a bare domain, which is the `didwebvh-rs` mapping. A server-managed mint names the server and says no action is needed. The exact URL is described rather than computed. Computing it would mean adding `didwebvh-rs` as a real dependency of `vta-cli-common` (it is only a dev-dependency of `vta-sdk`), or a new member on a published wire type — both out of proportion to one line of output, and the finding asked only that the output say serverless means *you* host it. Two similar messages in `vta-service` (the offline `vta did-webvh` path and the setup wizard) are left as they are: different surfaces, the first already names the exact URL, and neither is what was reported.

## `vta-service`
## [0.37.1](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/compare/vta-service-v0.37.0...vta-service-v0.37.1) — 2026-09-21 ### Fixed - **trust-tasks**: Name an upstream failure as one, not as an internal error ([#1609](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1609)) A `ServiceError` at 502/504 — a DID-hosting server or other peer that did not answer or refused — fell into the catch-all arm and went out as an opaque `internalError`. An openvtc join that failed because the hosting server's replies were refused by its mediator (`e.p.limits.queue.sender`) showed the user "internal error: the consumer could not complete this task", pointing at their own VTA. It now goes out as `taskFailed` with `details.reason` = `upstream_unavailable` and fixed text. The cause (peer, URL, its body) stays in the operator's log, as the framework requires. The SDK recovers the reason as `VtaError::Server { status: 502 }`, the variant REST already produces for the same failure.

title: fix(onboard): an added agent is stored when it connects, not when the encrypt prompt is left
body:
fix(onboard): an added agent is stored when it connects, not when the encrypt prompt is left

Adding a second agent from the setup page's "+ Connect another trust
agent" looked like it worked and left the list unchanged. A successful
connect held the connection in component state until the operator
clicked Encrypt or Skip on the "Wallet onboarded" screen. That screen
reads as the end, so people closed the tab there. The agent kept the
ACL entry and the offscreen document kept the holder key, but the
wallet never recorded the agent.

OnboardView now commits the connection as soon as connect succeeds. The
encrypt prompt is an optional follow-up that only re-wraps the key.
Leaving it closes the add-another panel. The key can still be encrypted
later from the plaintext banner.

Two related ways the connection map lost data:

- Each extension page hydrated the persisted map once and wrote the
  whole blob back on every change. A page loaded before another page
  added an agent wrote its stale map over the new one. The store now
  rehydrates when storage.onChanged reports another page's write. Its
  own writes are recognised and skipped.
- The popup's transport refresh rebuilt the connection from a hand-picked
  list that omitted homeContext and agentScope. Any transport drift erased
  them, and the setup page then said "not recorded".
  withRefreshedTransports (store.ts) replaces only the three transport
  members.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

body:
> **Status (21 September 2026):** answers the credential maintainer's [review of PR #8](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-zkp-spec/pull/8#pullrequestreview-4003440190) (16 September). One commit on top of `main`. Evidence states unchanged; nothing adopted. Round 1 (shape) runs on [dtgwg-zkp-tf #23](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-zkp-tf/discussions/23) to 22 September.

**By review item**

1. **Where the ZK-openable commitment lives** — record 007 states the task force's preference: a verification method in the identifier's DID document, not a credential member; Integration gains *Identifier commitment profile* (WG-14).
2. **Can the requirement be a MUST** — yes, conditioned on the identifier's key profile; a secure-element key is outside the profile and takes the issuance-time attestation route (007, Integration).
3. **A record for cred-spec #38** — new primitive record **022**, blinded digest references: the five digest-valued members (plus `taskDigestMultibase` once cred-spec PR #56 merges), the two reference kinds kept apart, three placements with conjectured costs; the disposition stays on #38 (WG-15).
4. **File the `taskContext` change** — filed against dtgwg-cred-spec as its own issue (linked from 008's issuance line); 008 re-read against PR #56.
5. **Credential catalogue** — the Introduction names the seven types, each an `xref` into the credential glossary.
6. **Issuer conformance** — target 5 says this specification profiles the issuer-side requirement; the credential specification's Conformance is not extended.
7. **Document Status, not a date** — [DTG-CRED] pinned to a minimum compatible Document Status (0.4.0), read at `994a3d6`; this draft's own header is now `Version 1.0 / Working Draft 0.1.0`.
8. **Sections by title, glossary by xref** — 34 merged-PR citations in live record fields replaced by section titles; 22 `DTG_CRED` cross-references render and resolve today.

Question 2 of #23: the WD02 example set cannot satisfy 007 as it stands (an Ed25519 `did:key` carries no second verification method); that is now the first implementation's first finding, on the record.

Housekeeping: PR #8's description corrected — Round 1 runs on #23 (the #27 link was a deleted duplicate).

title: fix(vtc): an offline command run beside the daemon says so, and `admin invite` names its online twin
body:
Keyring finding VTI-16. Run while the daemon is up, `vtc admin invite` failed
with the storage engine's own words:

    Invite failed: store error: FjallError: Locked

From that, Keyring concluded that admitting a new administrator meant taking the
community offline. **It never did.** `POST /v1/admin/invites` mints the same
invite through the running daemon — its own docs say it "mirrors the `vtc admin
invite` CLI exactly" — and the admin console's access page already calls it. No
client and no error message ever pointed there.

This is the case CLAUDE.md's rule is written for: when the operator's real
intent maps to a different command, print that command.

## The class, not the instance

fjall permits one process per data directory, and every offline `vtc` command
opens the store directly: `admin invite`, the three `acl` commands, `did-key`,
`sync-jobs`, and `status`. Each produced the same bare `Locked`.

`store::offline::open_offline` matches `fjall::Error::Locked` **exactly** and
returns `DaemonRunning { data_dir }`, whose message names the situation rather
than the engine. Every one of those commands now uses it. `admin invite`, the
one with an online twin, adds the no-downtime route and the body to send.

`vtc status` used to catch *every* open failure and guess "is VTC already
running?" — so a permissions error or a damaged directory read as a running
daemon. It now reports which it actually is.

## Tests

`a_held_store_is_reported_as_the_daemon_running` holds the store open as the
daemon would and opens it again — the real lock, not a constructed error — which
is what establishes that a held store surfaces as `fjall::Error::Locked` rather
than assuming it. Plus the message naming the situation, and a free store
opening.

Not changed here: the daemon's own startup still `.expect`s the store, so
starting a second daemon on one data directory panics with `failed to open
store: Locked`. Related, but a different surface from the one reported.

invite` CLI exactly" — and the admin console's access page already calls it. No
client and no error message ever pointed there.

This is the case CLAUDE.md's rule is written for: when the operator's real
intent maps to a different command, print that command.

## The class, not the instance

fjall permits one process per data directory, and every offline `vtc` command
opens the store directly: `admin invite`, the three `acl` commands, `did-key`,
`sync-jobs`, and `status`. Each produced the same bare `Locked`.

`store::offline::open_offline` matches `fjall::Error::Locked` **exactly** and
returns `DaemonRunning { data_dir }`, whose message names the situation rather
than the engine. Every one of those commands now uses it. `admin invite`, the
one with an online twin, adds the no-downtime route and the body to send.

`vtc status` used to catch *every* open failure and guess "is VTC already
running?" — so a permissions error or a damaged directory read as a running
daemon. It now reports which it actually is.

## Tests

`a_held_store_is_reported_as_the_daemon_running` holds the store open as the
daemon would and opens it again — the real lock, not a constructed error — which
is what establishes that a held store surfaces as `fjall::Error::Locked` rather
than assuming it. Plus the message naming the situation, and a free store
opening.

Not changed here: the daemon's own startup still `.expect`s the store, so
starting a second daemon on one data directory panics with `failed to open
store: Locked`. Related, but a different surface from the one reported.

title: fix(cli): a serverless mint says the operator must host it, and a hosted one says nothing
body:
Keyring finding VTI-20. `pnm did-mgmt dids create` returns the new DID's log
entry for **both** kinds of mint, and printed the same advice for both:

    To self-host this DID, place the log entry in a file named `did.jsonl`
    at the URL path corresponding to your DID URL.

That was wrong in each direction:

- **Serverless**, it read as one option among several, when it is the only way
  the DID will ever resolve. The VTA that minted it does not serve it; its URL
  answers 404 until someone publishes the file by hand.
- **Server-managed**, it told the operator to do something the hosting server
  had already done.

The advice now branches on `server_id`. A serverless mint says plainly that the
DID will not resolve until the operator publishes it, and where it goes — the
`--did-url` path, or `/.well-known/did.jsonl` for a bare domain, which is the
`didwebvh-rs` mapping. A server-managed mint names the server and says no action
is needed.

The exact URL is described rather than computed. Computing it would mean adding
`didwebvh-rs` as a real dependency of `vta-cli-common` (it is only a
dev-dependency of `vta-sdk`), or a new member on a published wire type — both
out of proportion to one line of output, and the finding asked only that the
output say serverless means *you* host it.

Two similar messages in `vta-service` (the offline `vta did-webvh` path and the
setup wizard) are left as they are: different surfaces, the first already names
the exact URL, and neither is what was reported.

title: feat(vtc)!: a community can ask an applicant to tell it about themselves
body:
Implements trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#543 (`trust-tasks-rs` 0.21.9). Design note §5.2.

A join manifest could only ask for credentials. A community that wanted a display name had nothing to put on the "what's required" screen, and nothing connected the join ceremony to an applicant's persona.

### Admin side
- **Storage:** a community-level row next to the branding (`community/requested-attributes`), backed up with it.
- **Admin routes:** `GET`/`PUT /v1/community/requested-attributes`.
  - Audited as `CommunityRequestedAttributesUpdated`, which records types added and removed, never values.
  - A type asked twice, or more than 32 entries, is refused.
- **Manifest:** published as `requestedAttributes` on `join-requests/manifest/0.2`.
- **Clients:** `VtcClient::requested_attributes` / `set_requested_attributes`, and `cnm vetting ask show|set --require/--optional/--purpose/--nothing`.

### Submit
`join-requests/submit/0.2` accepts `attributes`. The answers are checked before anything is stored, even before the open-request dedup, so an over-shared value is never written anywhere:
- **Missing:** a required type unanswered → `attributesMissing`.
- **Unrequested:** a type the manifest doesn't ask for → `attributesUnrequested`. Refused, not trimmed.
- Both carry `details.types`.

Accepted answers are stored on the request and returned by `show` and `list`. They're self-asserted and never fed to the join policy.

**Legacy REST route:** its holder signature covers a fixed set of fields that doesn't include `attributes`, so answers sent there would be unsigned. Answers therefore travel only on the Trust Task form. A community that requires one refuses the legacy route with `attributesMissing`.

### OpenAPI
- `vta_sdk::openapi::JoinManifest02RequestedAttribute` is rendered from the spec's own schema via a JSON pointer (`Name@<pointer>`), because the spec declares the item inline. This keeps the admin console types true to the spec instead of `Object`.
- `admin-ui/openapi.json` and `wire.ts` are regenerated.
- `JoinRequestAttribute` has no `deny_unknown_fields`. The published item is closed and has no `ext`, and the dispatcher's schema validation already refuses extra members.

**Breaking:** `vta_sdk::JoinRequestSubmitBody` gains `attributes`, and `vti_common::AuditEvent` gains a variant (the enum is `non_exhaustive`).

### Tests
- New end-to-end `requested_attributes_are_published_enforced_and_kept_with_the_request`, plus unit tests for the checks and the `cnm` flag parsing.
- VTC suite (`cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client`): 1723 passed.
- `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client`: 4687 passed.
- Clippy and fmt clean.
- Rebased onto `main` after the 0.46 release; the OpenAPI snapshot, response census and feature test were re-run and pass.

### Follow-ups
- **openvtc:** answering on join (a page to pick the face that answers, showing exactly what leaves, then a disclosure) is built on top of this and waits for its release.
- **Spec:** consider naming the requested-attribute item in the spec (`$defs.RequestedAttribute`), so the pointer form isn't needed.

title: fix(sdk): the vtc-host template advertises the REST base the VTC actually serves
body:
Keyring finding VTI-15. A VTC's DID document published

    { "type": "VTCRest", "serviceEndpoint": "{URL}" }

but `vtc-service` serves its API under `/v1`, so every request a client derived
from the document answered 405. Its sibling `VTCStatusList` has always carried
`{URL}{STATUS_LIST_PATH}`; `VTCRest` never got the equivalent.

## Why we never saw it

Nothing in this workspace consumes a `VTCRest` entry — `rest_url_from_did_doc`
looks for `vta-rest`. It exists for third parties, so a wrong value is invisible
here and costs only the integrator who trusts it. Keyring found it for that
reason, and it (with VTI-14, fixed in #1601) is why their repository carries its
own admin client.

That also corrects our remediation plan, which promised to "accept both forms on
the resolver side for DIDs already minted". There is no resolver side to make
tolerant.

## The fix

`REST_PATH`, an optional template variable defaulting to `/v1`, exactly as
`STATUS_LIST_PATH` already works — so a deployment serving the API elsewhere, or
at the root (empty string), can say so. The VTC setup wizard already passes
`URL` as the host base precisely to avoid a double `/v1` in the status-list
endpoint; its comment now covers both variables.

## Already-minted communities

A VTC's `did.jsonl` is write-once — it cannot re-sign its own log — so this
fixes new communities only. An existing one needs a VTA-side `dids edit` to
correct its `VTCRest` entry and a redelivered log. That is an operator action,
not something code here can do for them.

## Tests

The existing test pinned the bare URL; it now asserts `/v1` and says why, so the
value is not quietly reverted. A new test covers the override and the empty
root case, and that an empty `REST_PATH` leaves no trailing slash.
author: stormer78

title: feat(specs): declare outcome evidence for witness/session and vetting/session
body:
Registry half of outcome evidence: the declarations that let a relying party treat a cited witness or vetting exchange as completed. Until they exist, framework §4.9.4 check 3 fails for every citation.

**Depends on trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-spec#17, now merged** (2bdc08b). The framework text merged there is identical to what this PR copies into the `SPEC.md` mirror (`git diff aa5f94b 2bdc08b -- spec/` is empty), so the mirror is current.

## What changes

**`specs/spec.meta.schema.json`: new optional `outcomeEvidence` key.** It holds the declared response's Type URI, a binding in one of item 20.5's two forms, and a rationale. It lives in front matter for the reasons given on #17: a verifier can read it from the registry, it matches how `proofRequirement` and `retention` are already declared, and the lint can check it. The meta-schema is excluded from every binding generator (`NOT_PAYLOAD_SCHEMAS`), so there is no codegen, crate or package change. `npm run check-bindings` shows all four languages agree.

**`scripts/build-registry.mjs`: new `checkOutcomeEvidence` lint.** It fails the build when:
- the declared response doesn't exist in the registry, has no response payload (20.1), or doesn't require `proof` (20.2) or `issuedAt` (20.3) on the response;
- the declaring (opening) spec is a bearer spec, or has no REQUIRED `recipient` party (§4.9.4 check 4);
- a binding pointer names a member the payload schema doesn't declare (20.5). Pointers are checked as far as the schema can be followed; an opaque object or a `$ref` ends the walk.

It warns when the response's retention isn't `durable` (20.4 is a SHOULD). Negative-tested with a bad pointer and a missing response spec: both fail the build.

**The two declarations:**

```yaml
# witness/session/0.1
outcomeEvidence:
  response: https://trusttasks.org/spec/witness/session/submit/0.1#response
  binding: { id: /payload/vwc/taskContext, taskDigest: /payload/vwc/taskDigestMultibase }

# vetting/session/0.1
outcomeEvidence:
  response: https://trusttasks.org/spec/vetting/session/0.1#response
  binding: { challenge: { initiating: /payload/challenge, response: /payload/card/challenge } }
```

Vetting uses the challenge form, which 20.5.2 permits only where the party that opens the exchange must also issue the citing artifact. `vetting/session/0.1` requires exactly that: the statement's `issuer` is the session's `issuer`. The rationale field says so.

**`witness/session/submit/0.1`: cites §4.9.4 instead of its own pairing rule.** The old rule ("evidence issuer = credential issuer") matched the framework rule only because a witness both answers the session and issues the VWC. The spec now keeps just the checks particular to witnessing: the VWC's `issuer` is the session's `recipient`, and the credential's digest equals `vwcDigestMultibase`.

**`SPEC.md` mirror.** Per its canonical-source note, framework changes land in both places. This ports §4.9.4, §7.3 item 20, the *Outcome evidence* term, the §10 paragraph on the correlators outcome evidence discloses, and the `[VTI]` informative reference, with links converted to the mirror's numbered anchors.

## Checks
- `npm run validate`: 454 specs, "Outcome evidence (§7.3 item 20): 2 spec(s) declare outcomeEvidence", no errors.
- `npm run build`: clean.
- `npm run check-bindings`: all agree.
- No `version`, `Cargo.toml`, `package.json` or CHANGELOG edits (release-plz owns versions).

Evidence for the pairing rule and both bindings: [`ref-07g` @ eab6893](https://github.com/berkmancenter/keyring-wallet/tree/eab68939fc78e8f02094612c2e8433abfa65841f/tsp-reference/ref-07g-outcome-evidence-pairing).

title: Bind outcome evidence to its initiating document, not only by threadId (#17)
body:
Bind outcome evidence to its initiating document, not only by threadId (#17)

* Bind outcome evidence to its initiating document, not only by threadId

Follow-up to #15. Check 2 of "Evidence That a Cited Exchange Completed"
paired the terminal document with the exchange by threadId alone. A
threadId is not required to be unique, and the rule against carrying one
across exchanges binds conforming producers only, so a genuine success
response from an earlier exchange that reused the threadId with the same
counterparty passed all four checks for a later, cancelled one.

- Item 20.5: the governing specification declares a binding the
  response's own proof covers: the initiating document's id and task
  digest, or a fresh unguessable value it supplied (e.g. a challenge).
- Check 2 requires that declared binding in addition to threadId.
- Item 20 requires the initiating document to carry recipient, which
  check 4 depends on; bearer initiators cannot be cited.
- The empty-#response clause now defers to 20.1/20.5.
- The non-normative note records that witness/session and vetting/session
  do not yet declare, and which binding each already carries.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* Limit the fresh-value binding to issuer-initiated exchanges; root the pointers

From review on #17:
- Item 20.5's second form (a fresh value such as a challenge) relies on
  the initiator for freshness, the same producer-only guarantee check 2
  refuses for threadId. An initiator reusing both threadId and challenge
  passes (ref-07g case 9). Permit that form only where the initiator must
  be the issuer of the citing artifact; require id + task digest otherwise.
- JSON Pointers are evaluated from the Trust Task document root.

title: Bind outcome evidence to its initiating document, not only by threadId
body:
Follow-up to #15 (merged before review finished). This fixes three gaps in *Evidence That a Cited Exchange Completed* and Specification Requirements item 20. dtgwg-cred-spec#56 and dtgwg-vti-spec#33 both point at this section.

## 1. Check 2 paired the closing document with the exchange by `threadId` alone

A `threadId` is not required to be unique (§Naming an Exchange from Outside the Framework). The rule against carrying one across exchanges (Privacy item 2) binds conforming producers only, and §Binding a Citation already says a binding must not rely on that. **Failure case:** an initiator reuses a `threadId` with the same recipient. The genuine success response from exchange A then passes all four checks as evidence for exchange B, even though B was cancelled.

**Fix:** new **item 20.5**. The governing spec declares how the declared response is bound to the opening (initiating) document, as payload members named by JSON Pointer that the response's own `proof` covers. The binding is either:
- the opening document's `id` and its task digest, or
- a fresh, unguessable value that the opening document supplied, such as a presentation challenge.

Check 2 now requires that binding in addition to a matching `threadId`. Both existing ceremonies already carry one:
- `witness/session/submit#response`: its `vwc` carries `taskContext` and `taskDigestMultibase`.
- `vetting/session#response`: its `card` is presented against the session's freshly generated `challenge`.

**Evidence:** [`ref-07g` @ eab6893](https://github.com/berkmancenter/keyring-wallet/tree/eab68939fc78e8f02094612c2e8433abfa65841f/tsp-reference/ref-07g-outcome-evidence-pairing), Act 6. The seven original exchanges come out the same under both rules. The two reused-`threadId` cases (a generic exchange and the witness ceremony) are false positives under #15 and rejected here. Case 9, where the vetting initiator reuses both the `threadId` and the challenge, still passes. That's why the challenge form in 20.5 is limited to exchanges whose initiator must also issue the citing artifact (aa5f94b).

## 2. Check 4 depended on `recipient`, which is optional (MAY)

Item 20 required a proof on the response only. An opening document without a proof may leave out `recipient`, and check 4 then has nothing to compare against. **Fix:** item 20 now requires the opening document to carry `recipient`. An exchange opened under a bearer specification that names no recipient cannot be cited. Check 4 says it fails when `recipient` is absent.

## 3. Nothing declares outcome evidence yet, and this is the proposed fix

Under item 20, the declaration belongs to the spec governing the *opening* document. Today `witness/session/0.1` declares nothing (only `witness/session/submit/0.1` calls itself the outcome evidence), and `vetting/session/0.1` names no binding. Until they do, a consumer must treat every citation as not showing completion. That's the blocker. **Proposal to clear it** (a registry PR on dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf, opened once the wording here is agreed):

**(a) Where a declaration lives:** a new optional front-matter key, `outcomeEvidence`, in `specs/spec.meta.schema.json`, so a consumer reads the declaration from the registry rather than from prose. `spec.meta.schema.json` is excluded from every binding generator, so this means one schema edit and a lint rule, with no codegen or crate changes. Proposed lint: when `outcomeEvidence` is present, the declared response must have `proofRequirement.response: REQUIRED` and `issuedAtRequirement: REQUIRED`, and the opening role's party must be `member: recipient` and `requirement: REQUIRED` (20.2, 20.3, recipient).

**(b) The two declarations.** Both specs already meet every sub-item of item 20: a defined payload, proof REQUIRED on the response, `issuedAt` REQUIRED, `durable` retention, `recipient` REQUIRED. Only the declaration itself is missing.

```yaml
# specs/witness/session/0.1/spec.md
outcomeEvidence:
  response: https://trusttasks.org/spec/witness/session/submit/0.1#response
  binding:
    id: /payload/vwc/taskContext
    taskDigest: /payload/vwc/taskDigestMultibase
```

```yaml
# specs/vetting/session/0.1/spec.md
outcomeEvidence:
  response: https://trusttasks.org/spec/vetting/session/0.1#response
  binding:
    challenge:
      initiating: /payload/challenge
      response: /payload/card/challenge
```

What that gives each ceremony:
- **Witness:** the closing document is the `submit#response` signed by the witness, who is the `witness/session` `recipient` (check 4). It carries the VWC, whose `taskContext` and `taskDigestMultibase` name and bind the session document (check 2).
- **Vetting:** the closing document is the `vetting/session#response` signed by the applicant, who is the session's `recipient` (check 4). Its card copies the session's 32-byte one-time `challenge` verbatim (check 2). The card's own signature covers it as well as the envelope proof.

**(c) Also in that registry PR:** `witness/session/submit/0.1` stops stating its own "evidence issuer = credential issuer" pairing rule and cites the framework section instead, since that rule doesn't generalize to vetting.

**Recommendation: use the front-matter key, not prose.** A consumer checking completion has to find the declared response and its binding for whatever opening-document `type` it holds. A key gives it one place to look, readable straight from the registry. Prose would have to be read by a person and hand-coded into every verifier. The key also follows the pattern already set by `proofRequirement`, `issuedAtRequirement` and `retention`, which are declared the same way. And it lets the registry lint enforce item 20 (proof and `issuedAt` required on the declared response, `recipient` required on the opening document) instead of relying on review. The cost is small: `spec.meta.schema.json` isn't used by any code generator, so this is one schema edit plus a lint rule, with no generated-code or crate changes. Item 20 stays worded as "declare", and the registry's key is how a registered spec makes that declaration. Other registries stay free to declare it their own way.

## Also

The empty-`#response` clause now defers to 20.1 and 20.5: a fire-and-forget spec can be cited only by declaring a success response with a defined payload that carries the binding. This is a change from #15, where a proof alone was enough.

No Document Status bump; that stays in its own PR, as with #15. Rendered with `npm run render`: no errors.

@albertoleon7794 @bmiller59: this touches the section you wrote. Please check it against `ref-07g`. A reused-`threadId` exchange would be a good eighth case.

title: feat(messaging): add mediator queue, message, stats and traffic-monitor specifications
body:
Adds ten `messaging/*` tasks (all `0.1`, draft), so a messaging mediator can be operated entirely through Trust Tasks. An administrator can act across every account; an account controller can act on its own queues. These replace the REST `/admin/status`, `/purge` and `/queue/status` routes and the retired DIDComm admin protocols.

They are published together deliberately, so consumers pick them up from a single `trust-tasks-rs` release.

| Task | Who | Side effects |
|---|---|---|
| `stats/show` | admin | none |
| `queue/list` — ranked by count / bytes / oldest / saturation | admin | none |
| `queue/status` — optional per-counterparty breakdown | self or admin | none |
| `queue/purge` — peer and age filters, `dryRun` | self or admin (rootAdmin for privileged targets) | destructive |
| `message/list` — metadata only | self or admin | none |
| `message/get` — verbatim, undecrypted envelope | self, or rootAdmin | none; discloses `secret` |
| `message/delete` — per-id results | self or admin (rootAdmin for privileged targets) | destructive |
| `monitor/subscribe` / `unsubscribe` | self (own traffic only) or admin | mutating (lease) |
| `monitor/event` — one-way, `seq` plus heartbeat | mediator → subscriber | none |

**Traffic monitor.** A leased, filtered live tap on traffic metadata: stage, direction, channel, protocol (DIDComm or TSP), parties, size and refusal code. It never carries message bodies. Events are delivered live and never queued, and anything that cannot be delivered is counted rather than buffered. The spec requires that the monitor never slow down or fail the data plane it observes.

**Shared types.** Common shapes are in the new `messaging/_shared/0.1/mediator-ops.schema.json` component, which reuses `Vid` and `AccountType` from `messaging.schema.json`.

**Proof requirements.** Every request requires `proof` and `issuedAt`. The response to `message/get` also requires a proof, because the task discloses `secret`.

**Compatibility.** The change is additive: no existing spec or generated type changes. Rust, TS, Go and Dart bindings are regenerated.

**Checks run:**
- `npm run validate`: clean (464 specs)
- `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs --all-features`: green, including the new `rejects_invalid_examples` fixtures for `queue/purge` and `message/delete`
- `go build ./... && go vet`: clean

**Consumer.** The consumer is the Affinidi messaging mediator: affinidi/affinidi-tdk-rs, where the served-task registry refactor is the first step.

title: fix(persona): keep a face's name when it is saved here; take vta-sdk 0.46
body:
`vta-sdk` 0.46 (OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1605) adds an optional `slot` to every profile entry; `displayName` is what a face calls itself.

**The bug this prevents:** OpenVTC's face editor rebuilds live references from its tick list and writes them back bare. A slotted reference read as a tick would lose its name on the first save from OpenVTC. The loss is silent: the face still resolves, it just no longer says which name is its own.

**Fix:**
- A slotted reference is carried through untouched, the same way pinned and overridden entries already are. Only an unslotted one is the tick list's to rebuild.
- The sorting moved into `file_entry`. The existing test had its own copy of that logic, so it would have kept passing while the real code dropped the slot; it now calls the real function.
- New test: `a_slotted_reference_is_carried_through_not_rebuilt`.

**Dependencies:**
- `vta-sdk` 0.45 → 0.46.0.
- `vta-service` dev-dependency 0.36 → 0.37.
- The VTI crates in the lockfile move together, so a single `vta-sdk` resolves. `did-git-sign` still pulls 0.42.1, as before.

### Checks
All pass locally, matching `ci.yml`:
- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`
- `cargo test --workspace -- --include-ignored` (1479 passed, 0 failed)
- `--no-default-features` tests
- `dev-overrides` clippy and tests
- `arbitrary` check
- `cargo doc`

title: fix(join): say what an internalError and an upstream failure mean
body:
## Problem

A user's join failed at *Creating persona DID* with:

> ERROR: Failed to create persona DID: Failed to create DID via WebVH server: protocol error: trust task failed [internalError]: internal error: the consumer could not complete this task; the request itself was accepted

The real cause was upstream: the DID hosting server's reply was refused by its mediator (`e.p.limits.queue.sender`). But the screen pointed at the user's own VTA, and "the request itself was accepted" read as though something had half-happened.

## Change

`explain()` in `setup_sequence/vta.rs`, used by every DID-mint path including the join flow, adds one line per case:

- **`Protocol` containing `[internalError]`**: nothing was created; "accepted" only means well-formed; the cause is in the VTA's log (look for `trust task failed`). It also notes that an older VTA reports an unanswering hosting server this way.
- **`Server { status: 502 | 504 }`**: what a VTA with OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1609 sends for an upstream failure. It points at the service the VTA had to call (for a DID, the hosting server), not the request or the VTA.

The original error text is kept in both cases.

## Tests

`an_internal_error_says_nothing_was_created_and_where_the_cause_is`, `an_upstream_failure_points_at_the_service_the_vta_called`, `a_plain_protocol_error_gets_no_internal_error_note`; the `setup_sequence::vta` suite passes 10/10; clippy clean.

title: fix(trust-tasks): name an upstream failure as one, not as an internal error
body:
## Problem

A user's openvtc join failed at *Creating persona DID* with:

> trust task failed [internalError]: internal error: the consumer could not complete this task; the request itself was accepted

The VTA's own log had the real cause:

```
cause=bad gateway: `did:webvh:Qmbxds…:dids.ic3.dev` did not answer over TSP after re-establishing the relationship
```

The did-hosting log showed the path was reserved, but the reply was refused by the mediator (`e.p.limits.queue.sender`). So the fault was upstream, yet the wire said "this VTA had an internal error". That's because `app_error_to_reject` sent every `ServiceError`, including the `bad_gateway_error` that every peer failure produces, through the opaque catch-all.

## Change

- `ServiceError` at **502/504** → `taskFailed`, `details.reason: upstream_unavailable`, with fixed text: *"a service this VTA depends on did not answer or refused the request; the VTA's log names which one and why"*.
- The cause is **still not put on the wire**. Bad-gateway messages can carry a peer's URL, its transport error, and (from `send_rest`) the peer's response body, which is the same class of detail the `Internal` arm withholds. It goes to the log at `error`.
- `vta-sdk`: new `trust_task_reject_reasons::UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE`; `trust_task_error` recovers it as `VtaError::Server { status: 502 }`, which is what `from_http` already gives a REST caller.
- Other `ServiceError` statuses stay opaque `internalError` (tested).

Additive on the wire. An older SDK sees `taskFailed` with a reason it doesn't know and falls back to `Protocol` (existing behaviour for unknown reasons). No version fields touched (release-plz owns them).

## Tests

- `an_upstream_failure_is_named_as_one_without_its_cause` (502 + 504; no URL/DID leak; not the internal text)
- `other_service_errors_stay_internal`
- `an_upstream_failure_arrives_as_a_bad_gateway` (SDK)
- `cargo test -p vta-service --lib trust_tasks`: 268 passed; `cargo test -p vta-sdk --lib`: 380 passed; clippy clean.

Companion: an openvtc PR that makes `explain()` say what both cases mean.

title: fix(trust-tasks): name an upstream failure as one, not as an internal error (#1609)
body:
fix(trust-tasks): name an upstream failure as one, not as an internal error (#1609)

A `ServiceError` at 502/504 — a DID-hosting server or other peer that did
not answer or refused — fell into the catch-all arm and went out as an
opaque `internalError`. An openvtc join that failed because the hosting
server's replies were refused by its mediator (`e.p.limits.queue.sender`)
showed the user "internal error: the consumer could not complete this
task", pointing at their own VTA.

It now goes out as `taskFailed` with `details.reason` =
`upstream_unavailable` and fixed text. The cause (peer, URL, its body)
stays in the operator's log, as the framework requires. The SDK recovers
the reason as `VtaError::Server { status: 502 }`, the variant REST
already produces for the same failure.

title: Define outcome evidence for a cited exchange
body:
The Trust Tasks half of splitting [trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec#18](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec/pull/18) across the three specifications, following the scope guidance in [dtgwg-cred-tf#39](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-tf/discussions/39) and the review on #18. The full redistribution map is in the credentials PR.

| Part | PR |
|---|---|
| Trust Tasks (this PR) | this one |
| Credentials | trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec#56 |
| VTI | trustoverip/dtgwg-vti-spec#33 |

**Merge order: this PR first.** dtgwg-cred-spec#56 links directly to the `#evidence-that-a-cited-exchange-completed` anchor this PR creates; merging it before this one leaves a dead link in a published Working Draft. The credentials and VTI PRs can merge in either order once this is in.

@talltree @sankarshanmukhopadhyay — tagging you as the authors of the #39 scope guidance this split implements. @stormer78 — item 20 below is where your three follow-ups from the trust-tasks-tf#173 closing comment land.

## Why here

Trust Tasks 0.5.0 already absorbed most of #18's reasoning through trust-tasks-tf#173: naming the innermost exchange by its initiating `id`, the task digest, `inResponseTo`, the document lifecycle. What it does not define is whether a **cited exchange completed**. That rule lives today in #18 and, separately, in `witness/session/submit/0.1` and `vetting/session/0.1` — none of which generalizes on its own.

Under the #39 scope guidance, a credential specification defines its types, properties and high-level requirements and references the specifications that define the rest; processing, ceremony and evidence requirements belong here.

## What this adds

- **Evidence That a Cited Exchange Completed** — four checks: the citation binds the initiating document; the terminal's `threadId` pairs through the initiating document; the terminal's type is the **declared** outcome-evidence response; it is signed by the initiating document's **`recipient`**.
- **Specification Requirements item 20** — a citable specification declares its outcome-evidence response, with a payload schema, proof REQUIRED, `issuedAt` required, and `durable` retention. This is where Glenn's three follow-ups from the #173 closing comment land: the `cancelled` terminal state, items 17 and 18, and the empty `#response`.
- **Privacy Considerations item 6**, the **outcome evidence** term, and VTI as an informative reference.

## Evidence

[Keyring `ref-07g-outcome-evidence-pairing`](https://github.com/berkmancenter/keyring-wallet/tree/c3a7f1d2a547d7a602cf93b87f5672d7a158d4c1/tsp-reference/ref-07g-outcome-evidence-pairing) runs seven exchanges — witness, vetting, a minted thread, a cancellation, a self-signed response, an error, a counterfeit — through the witness spec's rule, Keyring's verifier, #18's text, and this rule, using real Trust Task documents and `eddsa-jcs-2022` proofs. Only this rule gets all seven right.

| Exchange | witness spec | Keyring | #18 | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| witness ceremony | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ false negative | ✓ |
| vetting ceremony | ✗ (out of scope) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| minted `threadId` | ✗ (out of scope) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| cancelled (control `#response`) | ✗ | ✓ false positive | ✗ | ✗ |
| holder-signed `#response` | ✗ | ✓ false positive | ✗ | ✗ |
| error / counterfeit | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ | ✗ |

The two false positives are a Keyring bug, tracked on our side, not a change proposed here.

## Notes for review

- `witness/session/submit` and `vetting/session` stay consistent with this section for their own exchanges; the registry specs are not edited here. `witness/session/submit/0.1` still states its own pairing rule ("evidence issuer = credential issuer"), which agrees with this general rule only because the witness case makes issuer and recipient coincide — a follow-up issue on dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf will propose it cite this section instead.
- **No Document Status bump** — bumps have been their own PR. A follow-up will bump it and fill in the minimum-version notes that dtgwg-cred-spec#56 and dtgwg-vti-spec#33 currently record as pending.
- Rendered with `npm run render` — no errors.
- Reviewed internally on our fork before proposing here; @bmiller59 is credited as co-author for the material carried over from his review.

title: Define outcome evidence for a cited exchange, once (#15)
body:
Define outcome evidence for a cited exchange, once (#15)

Binding a Citation to the Document It Names fixes which exchange a citation
names, but not whether that exchange completed. The DTG credential
specification's taskContext binding depends on that second question, and the
rules for it currently live in cred-spec PR #18 and, separately, in the
witness/session/submit and vetting/session task specifications. This moves
the generic rule into the framework, as the working group's scope guidance
places ceremony and evidence requirements here.

- New section, Evidence That a Cited Exchange Completed: the four checks a
  consumer relying on a citation performs — the citation binds the initiating
  document; the terminal document's threadId pairs through the initiating
  document (so a minted threadId does not orphan evidence); its type is the
  declared outcome-evidence response (so a control response, error, or
  next-step never reads as completion); and it is signed by the initiating
  document's recipient (so a self-signed response does not pass, and vetting,
  where the responder is not the credential's issuer, still does).
- Specification Requirements item 20: a specification whose exchanges may be
  cited declares its outcome-evidence response, with a payload schema, proof
  REQUIRED, issuedAt required, and durable retention — the declarations Glenn
  Gore identified on trust-tasks-tf#173 as belonging to this profile.
- Privacy Considerations item 6: outcome evidence discloses the exchange's
  correlators, so unlinkability is assessed across the composition.
- New term, outcome evidence; VTI added as an informative reference.

The non-normative note records why each check is needed. Every case in it is
exercised against real Trust Task documents and proofs in Keyring's
tsp-reference/ref-07g-outcome-evidence-pairing.

Refs trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec#18, trustoverip/dtgwg-cred-spec#11,
trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#173.

title: trust-tasks-rs-v0.21.9
body:
### Added

- **vtc**: A community can ask an applicant to tell it about themselves ([#543](https://github.com/trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf/pull/543))

From the persona context-first design note (verifiable-trust-infrastructure,
  docs/05-design-notes/persona-context-first.md §5.2): a join manifest could
  ask only for credentials, so a community wanting a display name and a
  country had nothing to put on the "what's required" screen, and nothing
  connected the join ceremony to the applicant's persona.

  All additive, no new versions:

  - vtc/join-requests/manifest/0.2: optional `requestedAttributes` --
    claim types (never values), each `required` (default true) with a
    `purpose` shown to the applicant. Outside every criterion, so no
    requirementsDigest covers it. Answers are self-asserted: a community
    MUST NOT describe one as verified or decide as if it were; a community
    needing an attested value asks for a credential instead.
  - vtc/join-requests/submit/0.2: optional `attributes` -- [{type, value}],
    bound to the applicant by the document proof. New codes
    attributesMissing (a required one is absent) and attributesUnrequested
    (a type the manifest does not request -- refused rather than stored, so
    an over-sharing client cannot leave data with a community that never
    asked). SHOULD be sent through the applicant's own disclosure path so
    their record of what they told whom includes it.
  - vtc/_shared JoinRequest: optional `attributes`, so show and list carry
    the answers to reviewers, as the applicant's own statement.

  Bindings regenerated in Rust, TS, Go and Dart.

title: vta-service-v0.37.0
body:
### Added

- **persona**: Keep a pinned value through an edit, and let the holder purge it ([#1606](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1606))

Implements the retention half of trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#538
  (design note docs/05-design-notes/persona-context-first.md §9.1).

  A pin ({ref, pinVersion}) is for the counterparty who verified a value
  and must keep being shown it -- after a name change, the bank that has
  not been told yet. The store did not keep the version an edit replaced,
  so a pin resolved stale from the first edit onward: pinning worked only
  until the one event it exists for.

  Retained by reference (new vta-persona `retention` module, `pav:` keys):
  - An edit keeps the version it replaces when a face pins it, and a pin
    is served from that copy.
  - A kept version is reaped the moment no face pins it (after profile put
    and delete); an edit nothing pins keeps nothing.
  - Deleting the attribute drops every kept version with it.
  - Attribute.retained_versions lists what is kept and the faces pinning
    it, on attribute/list; filled on read, never stored.
  - A face pinning a kept version still presents that value, so the
    correlation index counts it among what the face carries, and a face's
    own analysis treats such a pin as carried rather than as the live
    attribute.

  The holder's override: persona/attribute/purge-version/1.0 removes kept
  versions (named, or all), re-pushes and names every face that pinned one
  (stalePins). Those faces present the entry as stale -- never the current
  value, which the holder did not choose for that counterparty. The current
  version is refused (currentVersion); that is attribute/delete. New
  PersonaStore::purge_versions, VtaClient::persona_attribute_purge_version,
  `pnm persona attribute purge-version`.

  profile/put now refuses a pin to a version neither current nor kept with
  the spec's pinnedVersionUnavailable code, naming the pins, instead of
  storing a face that presents nothing for that entry.

- **persona**: Say which entry is a face's name — entry slots ([#1605](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1605))

* build: require trust-tasks-rs 0.21.8 for persona slots and kept versions

  0.21.8 publishes trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#538: the optional
  ProfileEntry and ResolvedClaim `slot`, Attribute.retainedVersions, the
  duplicateSlot codes, and persona/attribute/purge-version/1.0.



### Fixed

- **did-webvh**: Serialize versionTime log updates ([#1599](https://github.com/OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure/pull/1599))

* fix(did-webvh): serialize versionTime log updates

  Use one current-time policy for TEE genesis and runtime did:webvh
  updates. Wait for the next valid whole-second boundary, rechecking
  after wall-clock rollback, instead of backdating entries.

  Serialize same-DID log appends within a VTA process and add regression
  coverage for rapid updates, concurrent appends, legacy timestamps, and
  TEE genesis followed by an immediate validated update.

title: feat(vtc): a community can ask an applicant to tell it about themselves
body:
From the persona context-first design note in verifiable-trust-infrastructure (`docs/05-design-notes/persona-context-first.md` §5.2), discussed in trustoverip/dtgwg-htx-tf#11.

A join manifest could only ask for credentials. A community that wants a display name and a country had nothing to put on the "what's required" screen, and nothing connected the join ceremony to the applicant's persona.

All changes are additive; no new versions:

### `vtc/join-requests/manifest/0.2` — `requestedAttributes`
- Claim types from the persona claim-type registry, never values.
- Each entry has `required` (default true) and a `purpose` shown to the applicant before anything is disclosed.
- It sits outside every criterion, so no `requirementsDigest` covers it.
- **Answers are self-asserted.** A community MUST NOT describe one as verified or decide as if it were. A community that needs an attested value asks for a credential in a criterion instead.

### `vtc/join-requests/submit/0.2` — `attributes`
- `[{type, value}]`, bound to the applicant by the document proof.
- New error code `attributesMissing`: a required attribute wasn't answered. Details name the missing types.
- New error code `attributesUnrequested`: a type the manifest didn't ask for. Refused rather than stored, so an over-sharing client can't leave data with a community that never asked for it.
- A producer SHOULD send the values through the applicant's own disclosure path, so the applicant's record of what they told whom includes them.

### `vtc/_shared/0.1` `JoinRequest` — `attributes`
Carries the answers through `show` and `list` to reviewers, as the applicant's own statement.

### Checks
- `npm run validate`
- `npm run check-bindings`: all four languages agree
- `cargo build --workspace --all-targets`
- `cargo test -p trust-tasks-rs`
- Bindings regenerated in Rust, TS, Go and Dart

title: feat(persona)!: keep and show what a community may call a face
body:
Adopts `vta-sdk` 0.45 (OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1597).

### What changes
- **The label is carried forward.** `persona/binding/set` replaces the whole binding, label included, and OpenVTC has no way to set a label. Without this, changing a face from OpenVTC would silently erase the name the holder gave the community in `pnm` or the console. So `persona::binding::set` now reads the current label and sends it back. If that read fails, the write fails too, rather than defaulting to no name.
- **Both names are shown.** The panel line now reads `wears: <your name> (N attributes) — known here as “<label>”`. The agent now gives the face's own name only to the holder (which OpenVTC is), and gives the community the label.

### Dependencies
- `vta-sdk` 0.43.1 → 0.45.0, and the `vta-service` dev-dependency 0.32 → 0.36, so the graph resolves a single `vta-sdk`.
- The lockfile also updates the VTI subsystem crates and `vtc-client` to releases that require `vta-sdk ^0.45`. `vtc-client` 0.6.7 was keeping a second copy, `vta-sdk` 0.42, in the graph.
- `did-git-sign` still pulls `vta-sdk` 0.42.1, as it did before this PR.
- A test fixture gains the `sub_contexts` field that `vta-sdk` 0.44 added.

### Checks
Everything in `ci.yml` except bench, coverage and the plain `cargo check`:
- `cargo fmt --all --check`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test --workspace`: 1459 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo test --workspace --no-default-features`
- `cargo clippy -p openvtc --all-targets --features dev-overrides -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test -p openvtc --features dev-overrides`
- `cargo check -p openvtc-core --no-default-features --features arbitrary`
- `cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`

New test: `a_labelled_binding_says_what_the_community_is_told`.

### Update
- Takes `vta-sdk` 0.45.1 (OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1602). 0.45.0 reported a declared `vta/contexts/get:notFound` as a protocol error, which failed `community_context_e2e` under coverage (`--include-ignored`).
- Re-run locally:

  - `--no-default-features` and `dev-overrides` test runs pass
  - clippy clean in both configurations
